articles.title: El Celta quiere volver: espera un correoso Union Saint-Gilloise en la Europa League
articles.standfirst: Los célticos necesitan vencer al Union Saint-Gilloise para seguir con opciones en esta Europa League
articles.summary: Los célticos necesitan vencer al Union Saint-Gilloise para seguir con opciones en esta Europa League
articles.body: La derrota de la primera jornada de la fase de grupos de la Europa League, en Chipre ante Omonia Nicosia, sigue pasando factura al Celta, que pese a su victoria en Glasgow sigue fuera de los 24 equipos que continuarían en el torneo. Un triunfo este jueves ante el Union Saint-Gilloise mejoraría esa situación, cuando se llega al ecuador de la fase. No será sencillo, el rival suma siete puntos en las tres primeras jornadas, no conoce la derrota y es sexto clasificado en la actualidad. Balaídos es clave para la clasificación continental. De momento el único partido disputado en Vigo, en la fase de grupos, finalizó con derrota en el descuento, ante la Juventus. Ahora encadenan dos partidos como locales, al de la Union Saint-Gilloise le seguirá otro de gran complejidad ante el Bournemouth. El margen de error se estrecha. Con el partido de este jueves, los equipos belgas pasarán a ser a los que más veces se han enfrentado los vigueses en Europa, al ser el noveno partido de un total de noventa y siete. La estadística les beneficia en los ocho anteriores, con tres victorias célticas y cinco empates. Nunca perdieron. Claudio Giráldez, dentro de sus habituales rotacione, presentará un once lo más cercano a un equipo base para esta nueva cita en el partido europeo. Un nuevo traspié en Europa como locales empinaría la cuesta clasificatoria, pero desde dentro del conjunto vigués se encuentran motivados para poder hacer valer su superioridad y dejar los tres puntos europeos en territorio gallego. El Celta está preparado. .l

articles.title: Wrexham news: Phil Parkinson's pride as Wrexham deliver against Middlesbrough
articles.summary: Phil Parkinson spoke about the pride he took from Wrexham's display as they secured a 2-0 win over Championship leaders Middlesbrough at the Racecourse Ground.
articles.body:
Phil Parkinson feels his Wrexham side delivered a performance the club's fans, staff and owners could relate to as they defeated Championship leaders Middlesbrough 2-0 at the Racecourse Ground.

Second half goals from George Thomason and Ollie Rathbone earned the Red Dragons a crucial victory as Boro's 11-game unbeaten league run was ended.

It was the perfect response from Wrexham on the back of what was a lacklustre display against Sheffield United at Bramall Lane five days earlier.

"As I said to you after the game on Friday, all I ever want and all the owners want is the honesty in the performance which our fans can relate to," said Parkinson.

"That's why there's been a great connection between the supporters and the players, owners and myself because, in general, they've seen honesty and commitment and that's what the club's all about.

"I'm just really pleased. We're not getting carried away, but we upset a good team tonight."

The Wrexham boss added: "Middlesbrough know they've been in a game tonight.

"My, Steve [assistant coach, Parkin] and the rest of the staff's mantra since day one is that if anyone comes to the Racecourse, they've got to know that they've been in one hell of a game, and I think the Middlesbrough players know that tonight."

Speaking in his post-match press conference after the victory over table toppers Boro, Parkinson - a boyhood Middlesbrough supporter - revealed his father has recently been unwell.

The 58-year-old boss paid a touching tribute to his father in the aftermath of the victory.

"I'd just like to make a special mention to my dad, he's been ill over the last few weeks," he explained.

"I know how much that performance will have lifted him tonight, watching back home in Stockton-on-Tees with a lot of his friends, Middlesbrough fans as well.

"I just can't wait to speak to him on the way back."

Wrexham stun leaders Boro to earn crucial victory

Wrexham suffer 'significant' Smith injury blow

Sam Smith was absent from the matchday squad for the victory over Kim Hellberg's side.

The striker sustained a knee injury in the latter stages of Wrexham's 1-0 loss to Sheffield United at Bramall Lane on Friday night.

Prior to the win against Middlesbrough, Parkinson confirmed the 28-year-old was set for a spell on the sidelines.

In the aftermath of the contest, the manager revealed Smith is set to undergo surgery next week and will be sidelined for the remainder of the campaign.

"Unfortunately with Sam, he's done his cruciate," Parkinson added.

"He's going to be out for nine months and faces the operation next Wednesday."

Wrexham have been dealt numerous injury issues this season, with Josh Windass, Nathan Broadhead, Liberato Cacace and Callum O'Hare among those currently sidelined.

But Parkinson said he would not accept players feeling sorry for themselves, something he felt may have been the case at Sheffield United last time out.

"We've had injuries in other years, we've had setbacks, we've always dug deep," Parkinson said.

"I felt at Sheffield United we looked like a team that had almost taken one blow too many, but I'm not accepting that."

articles.title: An Introduction to Dinamo Zagreb: What Can Sunderland Expect?
articles.summary: Ahead of tonight’s Europa League encounter, Dan Knighton has a look at what we can expect from our Croatian visitors.
articles.body:
Tonight, Sunderland play their second Europa League home game of the campaign, as the Lads welcome Dinamo Zagreb to Wearside. Here's what you need to know about the Croatian champions!

With a population of around 750,000, Zagreb is Croatia's largest city, and the use of its name dates back nearly 1000 years to 1094 AD.

The city emerged from two medieval settlements (Gric and Kaptol) and began rapid development and expansion when the two combined in the 19th century.

It has played a crucial role in the political history of Croatia, and in 1941 it became the capital of a Croatian puppet state controlled by the Axis powers. After being freed in 1945, Croatia became a part of Yugoslavia from the end of the Second World War until 1991. Zagreb was the centre of a newly independent Croatia during and following the Croatian War of Independence (1991-1995).

On a lighter note, Zagreb is home to the world's shortest public transport funicular, which connects the city's old town to its newer Novi Zagreb area. It spans a total of 66m, and between its opening in 1890 to 1934, it was powered by steam. Nowadays, the journey is electrified and lasts approximately a minute.

The city also keeps many of its old traditions. Every day at noon, a cannon is fired from Lotrščak Tower beside the funicular to mark midday. This has happened every day since 1877. Zagreb also has over 200 gas street lamps which are still lit manually every night, and this tradition dates back to 1863.

There are also a number of weird and wonderful museums to visit in the Croatian capital. These include the Museum of Hangovers, the Museum of Laughter, the Museum of Broken Relationships, and a mushroom museum.

Dinamo Zagreb were initially formed in 1911 when Croatia was a part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. Upon the end of the Second World War, the club was dissolved by communist authorities; however, it was re-established just three days later on the ninth of June, 1945.

The new club inherited the colours, nickname, badge and fanbase of the original club. Its name was changed to Croatia Zagreb in 1993 – a move which was seen as a political move to move away from the club's communist past amidst Croatian independence. However, this name was never accepted by supporters, and the name Dinamo Zagreb was reinstated in the year 2000.

Dinamo Zagreb is Croatia's most successful club and has lifted the Croatian league 25 times, most recently last season, in which they finished 20 points ahead of second-placed Hajduk Split.

They have also won the Croatian Cup and Super Cup a record 18 and eight times respectively, as well as nine Yugoslav League titles and eight Yugoslav Cups pre-1991.

Over the years, Dinamo Zagreb have had a massive number of incredibly talented players wear their famous blue shirts.

Former Ballon D'Or winner Luka Modric started his professional career with Dinamo Zagreb. Aged just 18, Modric signed a ten-year contract and made a total of 94 league appearances for the club, scoring 26 league goals in that time.

After three successive Croatian League titles and two cup triumphs, he departed to Tottenham in 2008 before cementing his place as an all-time great at Real Madrid. Modric now plays for AC Milan and could face Sunderland in December at the San Siro.

Many of the Croatian golden generation team that reached the final of the 2018 World Cup played for Dinamo Zagreb, aside from Modric. This includes Mario Mandzukic, Dejan Lovren, and Marcelo Brozovic.

Current Manchester City duo Mateo Kovacic and Josko Gvardiol also started their careers at Dinamo Zagreb. Dani Olmo, World Cup winner with Spain this summer, joined Dinamo Zagreb as a sixteen-year-old from Barcelona's academy and made 80 league appearances before moving on to RB Leipzig.

Former Arsenal and West Ham striker Davor Suker also spent two years of his career in the Croatian capital, where he averaged over a goal every other game.

The Maksimir Stadium was built in 1912 and has been the home of Dinamo Zagreb since.

Currently, it is operating at a reduced capacity of around 25,000 after damage from an earthquake in 2020 forced the closure of a stand. Before this, capacity was around 35,000.

It has also hosted a plethora of international matches, most recently a meeting between Croatia and Montenegro in September 2025.

The Bad Blue Boys is the name of Dinamo Zagreb's notorious 'ultras' supporters group.

The group formed in 1986, and quickly after their formation, they developed a strong pro-Croatian independence stance amidst the changing political backdrop in the lead-up to the breakup of Yugoslavia.

They have been involved in a number of controversies over the years and have faced punishments for their behaviour, including stadium bans and fines. However, the Bad Blue Boys have used their influence for good. Following the earthquake in 2020 that damaged the Maksimir Stadium, the group quickly mobilised and helped to organise and distribute humanitarian aid, as well as helping to rebuild a hospital.

Ahead of our meeting tonight, Dinamo Zagreb currently sit second in the Croatian League – four points behind leaders Hajduk Split but with a game in hand.

Our visitors will be managerless, having sacked manager Mario Kovacevic after a shock 1-0 defeat to Rudes in the league. Kovacevic had been in charge for 73 matches and won 48 of those, overseeing last season's league and cup double in the process.

Dinamo Zagreb currently sit on four points from their three Europa League games so far. They kicked off their European campaign with a 0-0 draw against Hapoel Beer Sheva, then beat Anderlecht at home courtesy of a last-minute penalty. In their last Europa League outing, they lost 4-2 at home to Dutch side NEC Nijmegen.

Striker Dion Bejlo has started this season in electrifying form, so he will be one to watch tonight. In ten league games so far, he has scored 12 goals and registered five assists – an average of a goal contribution every 49 minutes in the league.

He scored both goals against NEC Nijmegen and converted the penalty against Anderlecht. He didn't feature against Hapoel Beer Sheva, so he has scored three goals in two Europa League games so far.

Beljo also scored a total of 38 goals last season – 31 in the league, two in the cup and five in the Europa League. In addition, he scored his first international goal against Spain during the last international break. Standing at six foot five at just 24 years old, he could be in line for a move to one of Europe's bigger leagues in the near future.

Our hopes of getting a positive result against Dinamo Zagreb may depend on our ability to keep Beljo quiet!

Former Southampton winger Mislav Orsic plays for our visitors. Scott McKenna, a Scottish international, formerly of Nottingham Forest, also plays for Dinamo Zagreb, although he is likely to miss the game through injury.

articles.title: Match Preview: Sunderland v Dinamo Zagreb — More European Fireworks On Wearside
articles.summary: Can we remain unbeaten in Europe?!
articles.body:
TV/Stream: Full live match coverage is available via TNT Sports.

Radio: Full live match commentary available via BBC Radio Newcastle (not online)

It feels like a long time since we took on AZ Alkmaar to bring European football back to Wearside, but this's our second night of fireworks at the Stadium of Light, and it falls on Bonfire Night.

A lot has happened since then. One thing that hasn't happened, however, is a Premier League victory. Just one point from a possible 15 has been taken since we kicked off our continental adventure on home soil.

Unfortunately, it has the potential to take the shine off our performance so far in the Europa League, and until we improve, any European game will be placed into the context of the two league games either side of it. But here we are, 9th in the table and on the same points as Juventus; we're still unbeaten, and we've got a great chance of progressing to the knockouts.

The news this week has been mixed since our capitulation at Coventry at the weekend. Let's go with the bad news first, and Habib Diarra has been ruled out for around six weeks. You feel for the lad to start with because he just can't catch a break, and then there's the aspect that he was a player who potentially gave us an option to freshen things up either tonight or at the weekend.

But, for all of those chanting his name recently, Chemsdine Talbi has replaced him in the European squad. Again, all eyes will be on the starting line-up, not just for tonight, but for clues of what we'll do at the weekend.

Our opponents tonight are Croatian champions Dinamo Zagreb, and they sacked their manager this week, which might mean a lot of our scouting reports go in the bin. They've beaten Anderlecht, drew against Hapoel Be'er Sheva and lost against NAC Nijmegen.

On the domestic front, they have won the league 19 times in the last 21 seasons. Which is pretty impressive. Last season, they reached the knockout phase, but were beaten at the first hurdle by Genk during extra time in the second leg. The year before last, they narrowly missed out on the knockout phase of the Champions League by goal difference, where they beat AC Milan and Salzburg on the way.

We shouldn't expect it to go all our way tonight.

The bookies have the Lads at 4/9 to win the game, while Zagreb are 5/1 for the victory, and the draw is 17/5.

The bookies might fancy us for a routine victory tonight, but I think it's going to be a tough test. I think we'll come out on top, and if we do come out on top in a tough game, it might be exactly what we need to raise the levels for the weekend.

articles.title: Brent Venables Says Everything Is on the Table After Firing Ben Arbuckle
articles.summary: Oklahoma coach Brent Venables fired second-year offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle on Monday and made Jason Witten the interim play caller, per ESPN. Asked w...
articles.body:
Oklahoma coach Brent Venables fired second-year offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle on Monday and made Jason Witten the interim play caller, per ESPN.

Asked whether John Mateer remains the starting quarterback, Venables said everything is on the table before Saturday's game at Florida.

The Sooners are 4-4 overall and 2-3 in the SEC, a year after reaching the College Football Playoff.

Venables Wants Points Any Way the Sooners Can Find Them

"Put incredible pressure on the defense and take care of the football," Venables said Tuesday, a day after making the move. "Score however you need to score, throwing it, running it, all of it. That's literally what we want."

He spoke at his weekly availability with Oklahoma 4-4 overall and 2-3 in the Southeastern Conference, one year after the Sooners made the College Football Playoff. Reporters wanted to know whether fifth-year senior transfer John Mateer stays at quarterback and what changes with Witten calling plays. Venables answered that everything is on the table and that everybody has a fresh slate.

What Venables Said About the Quarterbacks

Mateer, junior Whitt Newbauer and freshman Bowe Bentley have all taken practice reps this week. Mateer arrived from Washington State before last season with Arbuckle.

Venables offered his own diagnosis of the season. "Obviously, we didn't make the improvement," he said. "We played inconsistently. We lead the world in the turnover margin. We're on the wrong side of it. We've got to have better, more consistent quarterback play."

Venables chose not to go further on Arbuckle's departure or on Mateer's status. Quarterback jobs are under scrutiny elsewhere in the SEC too, where Nick Saban said the bench can motivate Texas quarterback Arch Manning.

"We want to win … and that takes everybody," he said. "That expectation hasn't changed whatsoever and we want to win this week and we want to win the next week and the week after and so forth."

Oklahoma fired Arbuckle after a 42-25 home loss to South Carolina in which the Sooners gathered only 118 total yards and no offensive touchdowns through three quarters. Mateer then threw two touchdown passes.

The season totals tell the same story. Oklahoma ranks 111th of 138 FBS teams at 336.9 total yards per game and 108th at 22.0 points per game. Last year's 10-win team produced 354.3 yards and 26.2 points. In 2024, Washington State ranked sixth nationally at 36.6 points per game and gained 442.8 yards per game with Arbuckle and Mateer, before the pair moved to Norman.

"My focus with you all today is really about what we've got to do this week to win and what that looks like here over the next four weeks," Venables said. "Incredibly important that we get someone to come in here and help us score touchdowns."

Witten joined the staff in January as tight ends coach. Before that he went 44-7 with two state championships over five seasons as head coach at Liberty Christian, a private school in Argyle, Texas. He moved into coaching after his final NFL season in 2020, having played 17 seasons, all but one with the Dallas Cowboys, and earned 11 Pro Bowl selections and four All-Pro selections. The Texas Sports Hall of Fame inducted him in 2019.

Across 2023 and 2024, the Warriors went a combined 26-1 and averaged 50.9 points per game. Liberty Christian plays in TAPPS, the private school version of Texas high school football, and in Witten's final season the Warriors went 1-2 against public school competition. His son Cooper, a five-star linebacker in the Class of 2027, plays at Liberty Christian and is committed to Oklahoma.

Venables put his trust in Witten plainly. "He's got an incredible wealth of knowledge and his communication skills are elite," he said. "He's built trust and real relationships with our entire staff but also the players, which is important. They're going to follow people that they believe in. He makes people better with his passion, his energy, his details, his readiness, his toughness, all of those things. He's elevated several parts of our program in a very short amount of time."

Oklahoma travels to Florida (5-3) on Saturday, then closes the season against Ole Miss, Texas A&M and Missouri. Three of the remaining matchups come against AP Top 25 competition. LSU and Alabama also meet on Saturday, and Lane Kiffin joked about the 2:30 kickoff the SEC gave them.

Nebraska coach Matt Rhule vowed he will not quit after his own team's third straight loss. At Oklahoma, the first answer arrives Saturday: who starts at quarterback, and what Witten calls.

Venables set the standard on Tuesday: score, and protect the football. The next four weeks will show whether a new voice on the headset changes anything.

articles.title: 'It's not a defeat, it's a lesson' - Red-eyed Michael Cuisance urges Lens team-mates to question themselves following record 9-1 Champions League loss to Como
articles.summary: Lens midfielder Michael Cuisance fought back tears as he called on his team-mates to take responsibility following Wednesday night's humiliating 9-1 Champion...
articles.body:
Lens midfielder Michael Cuisance fought back tears as he called on his team-mates to take responsibility following Wednesday night's humiliating 9-1 Champions League defeat at home to Como. Cesc Fabregas' Italian visitors produced a ruthless display in France to register the biggest away victory in the modern competition's history.

Emotional midfielder apologises to supporters

Cuisance cut a distraught figure after watching his side concede nine times on Matchday 4 as Como matched Bayern Munich's 2024 tally against Dinamo Zagreb for the highest single-game haul in the Champions League era.

Greek striker Tasos Douvikas hit a hat-trick after opening the scoring in the seventh minute, while Tenerife-born Nico Paz netted the third before half-time and held up a T-shirt honouring late striker Jesus de Miguel .

Speaking to Canal+ with red eyes, Cuisance said: "I'm speechless. The team needs to pull itself together, we need to do better. We're in the Champions League, we have to honour this European Cup, and today we weren't up to the task, we weren't good enough. We're sorry for the fans."

Humiliating collapse demands honest reflection

Captain Lucas Da Cunha, Marc-Oliver Kempf, substitute Mattia Liberali, Martin Baturina and 18-year-old Matteo Papaccioli - whose stoppage-time strike was confirmed by VAR - also scored around Ruben Aguilar's 65th-minute corner volley for the hosts. By winning by an eight-goal margin, the visitors equalled 8-0 victories recorded by Liverpool against Besiktas and Real Madrid against Malmo, while becoming the first side to score nine away in the European Cup since Feyenoord's 9-0 win at Olympiakos Nicosia in September 1971.

Urging his colleagues to show resilience after the rout, Cuisance added: "It's always upsetting; as a competitor, you never like to lose, whether by a small or large margin. It's not a defeat, it's a lesson. We have to learn from this, and we'll see what kind of character the team has. I think we're capable of it. I've experienced much worse in my life. Today, this has to be a lesson; we have to come away having learned something, and, as I said, there's only one way: learning, hard work, and everyone questioning themselves."

Competing in fourth-tier Serie D as recently as 2018-19, Como have been transformed since a 2019 takeover by London-based media firm Sent Entertainment, owned by Indonesian billionaires Robert Budi Hartono and Michael Bambang Hartono, who initially planned a television project screening young Indonesian players.

Having beaten RB Leipzig and Manchester United either side of losing to Feyenoord - who hold the overall European Cup record after beating Icelandic side KR 12-2 in September 1969 - Como sit fourth with 19 goals from four matches, matching Queens Park Rangers in the 1976-77 UEFA Cup.

Lens must now regroup quickly to restore their battered pride before returning to domestic action in Ligue 1 ahead of the upcoming November international break. Cuisance and his colleagues face a stern test of character as they attempt to prove they have learned from Wednesday's defensive capitulation before European duties resume later this month. Meanwhile, high-flying Como will look to carry their historic continental momentum back into Serie A this weekend.

articles.title: Amad: Man United attacker nominated for “prestigious honour”
articles.summary: Manchester United winger Amad has been nominated for a top award.YearThe Ivory Coast winger has had to transition from a right wing-back under Ruben Amorim t...
articles.body:
Manchester United winger Amad has been nominated for a top award.

The Ivory Coast winger has had to transition from a right wing-back under Ruben Amorim to a more attacking role under Michael Carrick over the last calendar year.

Last season he played 33 games, scoring two goals and providing four assists .

This year he started the season with a knock but has so far played seven matches, with zero goals and one assist to his name.

The 24-year-old has been in more productive form for his nation, impressing at the Africa Cup of Nations and the World Cup.

He scored three goals for his nation in the AFCON, scoring against Mozambique, Cameroon, and Burkina Faso.

The winger also found the back of the net twice in this summer's World Cup against Ecuador and Norway.

As a result, the club's official website reports, "Manchester United star Amad has been named on a 10-man shortlist for the CAF Player of the Year award. The prestigious honour for the best African footballer has only ever been won by two Ivory Coast internationals in the past – Didier Drogba and Yaya Toure."

The site also adds, "among the other contenders for the coveted prize are current holder Achraf Hakimi, Manchester City wide man Antoine Semenyo and Crystal Palace forward Ismaila Sarr."

The winner of the accolade will be announced on the 7th of December at a ceremony in December.

The Ivorian will be in action later this month for his nation as he has been called up to the squad for a double-header against Gambia in Africa Cup of Nations qualifying.

First, he will be needed for his club against Aston Villa on Sunday evening at Old Trafford.

articles.title: Enzo Maresca Issues Update on Gianluigi Donnarumma's Future After Latest Man City Error
articles.summary: Gianluigi Donnarumma: One of Man City's most divisive figures?More VideosManchester City had to take the lead on three separate occasions in eastern Germany...
articles.body:
Gianluigi Donnarumma: One of Man City's most divisive figures?

Manchester City had to take the lead on three separate occasions in eastern Germany on Wednesday night amid a spirited and testing showing from a Martin Demichelis-led RB Leipzig side.

Off the back of a 5-1 victory over AEK Athens on matchday three of the league phase, City knew that with a trip to Barcelona in December following a home clash with Napoli later this month, victory would likely be required to hold on to their top-eight place.

A Castello Lukeba own goal gave City the lead shortly before the half-time interval at the Red Bull Arena, before Ridle Baku would equalise shortly after the break. Enzo Fernandez regained the lead as he bulleted home a header from an in-swinging Iliman Ndiaye cross.

However, Antonio Nusa would bring the scoreline back level shortly after the hour-mark, before Erling Haaland would step up to score his 62nd UEFA Champions League goal in just his 61st appearance in the competition.

But the spotlight was placed on Gianluigi Donnarumma after the contest after several shaky moments once again between the sticks for the Manchester City No.1, including an error leading to one of Leipzig's strikes.

Highlighting Ridle Baku's equalising goal in particular, which took advantage of a gaping hole between Gianluigi Donnarumma and his near-post from a crossing position, Enzo Maresca was quizzed on whether the Italian's growing list of errors was now a 'concern'.

"It's not a concern, but it's a mistake," Maresca responded to reporters during his post-match media duties from the Red Bull Arena on Thursday night.

The Manchester City manager continued, "He recognises, he knows that it's a mistake. And now, in 48 hours, it's Nottingham Forest away [and] we need to be focussed on that. And then, we have an international break and we can see different things."

With the final international break of the calendar year firmly upon clubs across the globe, Enzo Maresca was further questioned on whether the pause from Manchester City action will act as an opportunity to reflect on matters - including the goalkeeping picture.

"I'm not thinking about the goalkeeper situation," Maresca doubled-down in defence of his mainstay first-choice shot-stopper.

"We're talking about a mistake, but a few minutes before, he's done a save that any keeper in the world, they're not going to do that save!

"So it's always a balance... And Gigio knows that the first goal was not good, but he's going to do better!"

One final test before the international break

Manchester City's players and staff must retain their focus on strong performance levels from their outing in Germany this week as they take on a final clash before the pause for international commitments in November.

Up next for Enzo Maresca and his players is a clash away at the City Ground to face Oliver Glasner's struggling Nottingham Forest side, hoping to bounce back from a narrow 0-1 home loss to Brighton & Hove Albion in the Premier League last time out.

Manchester City are due to arrive back in the north-west of England in the early hours of Thursday morning having departed Leipzig after the victory in Germany, with a recovery session due later in the day.

articles.title: 'A lot to improve going forwards' - Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya delivers honest verdict after Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres seal 2-1 win at Slavia Prague
articles.summary: Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya has admitted his side must sharpen up their second-half display despite holding on for a 2-1 Champions League victory away at S...
articles.body:
Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya has admitted his side must sharpen up their second-half display despite holding on for a 2-1 Champions League victory away at Slavia Prague on Wednesday night. First-half strikes from Noni Madueke and Viktor Gyokeres put the Gunners in control before the Czech hosts mounted a late fightback at the Fortuna Arena.

Raya warned his team-mates that they cannot afford to take their foot off the gas after surviving five minutes of stoppage time in the Czech capital on Matchday 4. Up at the other end of the pitch, 28-year-old Sweden striker Gyokeres seized his chance on his sixth start of the season as one of six changes alongside Ben White, Piero Hincapie, Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze. After setting up Madueke's ninth-minute opener and watching Tomas Holes poke wide, Gyokeres combined with Merino in the 38th minute to clip home off the far post.

Sloppy turnovers invite second-half pressure

That effort marked Gyokeres' first Champions League goal from open play since January against Kairat Almaty, while his only prior strike this season came in the Carabao Cup loss at Fleetwood, where teenager Max Dowman was sent off before making a late cameo on Wednesday. Although home keeper Nazar Domchak made several stops, including denying Madueke after link-up play involving Declan Rice and fit-again Christos Tzolis, Slavia registered 17 shots after the break.

Speaking to TNT Sports afterwards, Raya assessed the contrasting halves: "First half, we played really well, dominating the whole game and creating a lot of chances. I think we could have scored a few more goals. The second half was completely different, especially from them. They went up a gear. We were a little bit surprised and they made it really difficult for us. We need to learn from that. Delighted with the win, but a lot to improve going forwards."

On what changed after the break, he added: "They started pressing a little bit higher with a little bit more intensity. We had too many giveaways, especially in the final third, which meant we were running back towards our goal. We have to manage and dominate those actions and keep the ball to go for the third, fourth and fifth goals."

After Gabriel Magalhaes cleared substitute Ange N'Guessan's header off the line and VAR ruled Merino's challenge with Wiktor Nowak an accidental clash of heads, Raya pushed Oskar Kubiak's header onto the post before Nowak converted David Jurasek's 90th-minute cross.

Reflecting on his save at 2-0, Raya concluded: "It was really close, it was very similar to the last one against Bayern. I'm delighted to help the team that way. I'm just trying to do my job in the best way possible and keep clean sheets because we know that helps you to win a lot of games."

Claiming all three points lifted the reigning English champions up to third place in the Champions League table with 10 points from four outings. Fresh from edging Liverpool 1-0 last weekend and winning in Prague, Mikel Arteta's Premier League leaders now turn their focus back to domestic duties ahead of the November international break. The Gunners will welcome Hull City to north London on Saturday, November 7, for their Matchday 10 top-flight clash.

articles.title: Harry Kane: England captain and 2026 Ballon d'Or winner signs new contract at Bayern Munich running until 2029
articles.summary: England captain Harry Kane signs new two-and-a-half-year contract at Bayern Munich; the 33-year-old joined from Tottenham in 2023 and has scored 156 goals in 161 games for the Bundesliga giants; Kane became the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or in 25 years last month
articles.body:
The deal will see him remain with the Bundesliga giants until the summer of 2029.

Sky in Germany are reporting Kane's new salary is at least £20.9m (€25m) gross per year.

"I feel right at home at FC Bayern," Kane told the club's official website.

"I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich. We have a fantastic team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager. It makes me very proud to be part of this club.

"My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I'm now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club."

Kane has scored a phenomenal 156 goals in 161 matches since moving from Tottenham to Bayern in 2023.

His 73 goals for club and country last season - including six in the 2026 FIFA World Cup with England - helped him become the first English winner of the men's Ballon d'Or for 25 years.

During his time at Bayern, Kane has won two Bundesliga titles - the first in 2025 acting as the first major trophy of his career - as well as last season's German Cup and the German Super Cup in the last two years.

In the last three years, Kane has also won the European Golden Shoe twice - given to the top scorer on the continent - and has won the Bundesliga Golden Boot in each of his three seasons at Bayern.

Kane also took England to the Euro 2024 final during his time with the German giants, as well as leading the Three Lions to their best World Cup finish since 1966 earlier this summer.

Last month he equalled Peter Shilton's England appearance record by winning his 125th cap, which he will hope to beat in the upcoming Nations League matches.

Record-breaking Kane has 'a lot more left in the tank'

Analysis by Sky Sports News' Michael Bridge :

"Harry Kane, we've said consistently on Sky Sports News , is very happy at Bayern Munich.

"He's a real family man and they love living in Munich. He's a private man as well, he gets his privacy there and he's done incredibly well.

"At the end of the season when he spoke to Vincent Kompany - they thought if it wasn't for PSG they probably would have gone on to win the Champions League.

"I agree with that. They were absolutely outstanding last season. He's got a great relationship with the players and Kompany, you can see the goals, he's breaking records galore and the goals he scores as well.

"Listen to the Bayern Munich director saying they don't usually negotiate deals for players at this age. But I'm telling you this - he might be 33 but there's still a lot more left in the tank for Kane, there's absolutely no doubt about it."

articles.title: The hidden meaning behind Cristiano Ronaldo's new 'M' gesture as 1,000-goal milestone comes into view
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo's new 'M' gesture after scoring goals has sparked speculation among fans, suggesting a connection to his chase for the monumental 1,000-goal milestone. As he approaches this landmark, exploring the significance of his celebration and what it could mean for his legacy in football.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has spent much of his career making sure supporters know when he has scored, but his latest celebration has left them trying to decipher a different message. The Al Nassr forward has repeatedly appeared to form an 'M' with his fingers after finding the net, and fans believe the gesture could be a reference to the 1,000-goal milestone he is now chasing.Why Cristiano Ronaldo is making an 'M' with his fingersRonaldo's trademark 'Siu' celebration has become one of the most recognisable routines in football, but supporters have recently spotted him using a different gesture after scoring for Al Nassr. Rather than his usual celebration, the 41-year-old has been bringing his fingers together to form what appears to be the letter 'M'.The theory attracting the most attention, highlighted by the sports social media account 433, is that the letter represents 1,000 in Roman numerals. It is a plausible explanation given how close Ronaldo is to the landmark, although the player has not confirmed that this is what he intends.There is another detail that has caught supporters' attention. Al Nassr chief executive Jose Semedo has also celebrated alongside Ronaldo using the same gesture, prompting further speculation about whether it carries a message connected to the club's leading scorer.For now, its meaning remains unconfirmed. Ronaldo has not publicly addressed the celebration, so the Roman numeral explanation remains a theory rather than an official account.The timing, however, is difficult to overlook. Ronaldo scored his 983rd, 984th and 985th career goals in Al Nassr's 5-3 victory over Al-Kholood on October 29, taking his official tally to 985. As of October 30, 2026, he had reached that total in 1,343 senior appearances for club and country, leaving him just 15 goals short of four figures.Brazilian legend Pelé is the only player previously credited with scoring more than 1,000 career goals, having been credited with 1,279 between 1956 and 1977.Can Ronaldo score 15 goals before the end of 2026?Ronaldo has eight confirmed club matches remaining in 2026, giving him a limited number of opportunities to reach the milestone before the year ends. Al Nassr's schedule includes five Saudi Pro League fixtures against Al Qadsiah, Al Shabab, Al-Fayha, Al Hilal and Al-Fateh, alongside a King’s Cup tie against Al-Kholood on December 1.The club also have two AFC Champions League Elite matches remaining, against Al Sadd and Al-Gharafa. Should Al Nassr qualify for the knockout stage, those matches will take place from 2027.The schedule has changed following two major adjustments to Al Nassr's calendar. Their November 6 league match against Al-Hazem was officially postponed indefinitely, while the Saudi Super Cup fixture against Al-Kholood, scheduled for December 20, was moved out of the December window. The changes formed part of wider adjustments to domestic football calendars amid regional logistical changes and the rescheduling of the 2027 AFC Asian Cup.With 15 goals still required and eight club matches available, Ronaldo would need to average almost two goals per game to reach 1,000 before January. Scoring once in every fixture would leave him seven short, making the target a considerable challenge even with his recent hat-trick against Al-Kholood.He could also have opportunities with Portugal during the November international break. Ronaldo has been named in the preliminary squad selected by head coach Jorge Jesus for potential matches against Wales and Denmark, despite the reported fallout between the pair in September. His inclusion in the preliminary squad does not, however, guarantee that he will play in either fixture.If the 1,000-goal mark proves out of reach this year, Ronaldo could enter 2027 needing only a small number of additional goals, depending on how he fares during the remaining fixtures.What Cristiano Ronaldo has said about reaching 1,000 goalsRonaldo has previously described reaching 1,000 career goals as one of the major targets he still wants to achieve. Speaking in September, he called the prospect the 'cherry on top of the cake' and said he would particularly like to reach the milestone while representing Portugal.“It would be the cherry on the top of the cake to score my 1,000th goal with the national team. It would be the culmination of a beautiful story. I said I wanted to reach that target and I will reach that target. But I don’t have an obsession. If you are obsessed with something, you won’t get it … Just enjoy. Carpe diem, enjoy the day.”The Portugal captain has also made clear that his assessment of his own career will not depend on whether he reaches that figure. In a separate interview in October, he said that even a final tally below 1,000 would not change his belief that he is the greatest player in football history.“Things have to happen naturally. If I score 920 goals, or 925, or 930, the best player in history is me, and that’s the end of it.“The numbers speak for themselves. If I reach that figure, meaning a thousand goals, it would be something amazing and a target I am working towards, but I don’t think about the long term.”For now, Ronaldo remains 15 goals away from a milestone no other player has officially reached in the same way. Whether his new 'M' celebration is a deliberate reference to that target is still a question only he can answer, but supporters will have another reason to watch closely whenever he finds the net.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Ya es oficial: Vinicius es un problema deportivo para el Real Madrid"
articles.standfirst: Pablo Villa analizó en La Tribu de Radio MARCA el preocupante momento del brasileño
articles.summary: Pablo Villa analizó en La Tribu de Radio MARCA el preocupante momento del brasileño
articles.body: Pablo Villa ha sido contundente con la situación que atraviesa Vinicius Junior en el Real Madrid. En su opinión en La Tribu de Radio MARCA, el periodista ha analizado el rendimiento del brasileño tras el último compromiso europeo del conjunto blanco y ha puesto en duda su importancia actual dentro del equipo. "Ya es oficial: Vinicius Junior es un problema deportivo para el Real Madrid. Si quedaba algún resquicio para la duda, ayer volvió a quedar demostrado", aseguró. Villa señaló directamente la decisión de Mourinho de modificar el esquema que había funcionado hasta ahora, dejando a Arda Güler en Madrid y situando al brasileño en la banda izquierda. Una apuesta que, a juicio del periodista, no ofreció los resultados esperados. "Desdibujado, poco participativo, perdiendo 11 balones y sin haber completado ni un solo regate con éxito", describió sobre la actuación del extremo. Además, destacó su escasa incidencia en el encuentro, especialmente durante una segunda parte en la que apenas tuvo protagonismo, más allá de un autopase en el minuto 70 que Mbappé no consiguió culminar. Para Pablo Villa, el problema del brasileño va más allá de una mala actuación puntual. El periodista considera que el futbolista todavía arrastra las consecuencias de no haber conquistado el Balón de Oro en 2024. "Sigue sin despertarse de la peor pesadilla de su vida, el no Balón de Oro de 2024", afirmó. Una situación que, según su análisis, también se refleja en la actitud del jugador sobre el terreno de juego: "Se le nota en los gestos, en sus movimientos en el campo, Vinicius ya no cree en sí mismo". Villa también hizo referencia al cambio de jerarquías dentro del vestuario madridista. "Ha visto cómo Mbappé ha pasado a ser el gran estandarte del proyecto y un niño de 19 años le ha adelantado por la derecha y por la izquierda en cuatro ratos", señaló. El periodista recordó que Vinicius se había ganado su posición en el club gracias a su rendimiento, pero considera que la situación ha cambiado. "El club volvió a tenderle la mano cuando más dudas despertaba. Y el brasileño, lejos de responder a esa confianza, está volviendo a fallarle al escudo", lamentó. Pese a las dudas que genera su rendimiento, Pablo Villa reconoció que Mourinho continúa apostando por el brasileño, aunque cuestionó los motivos de esa confianza: "Mourinho le ha demostrado fe, aunque su apuesta suene más a obligación que a convicción". El periodista también quiso destacar la capacidad de reacción del Real Madrid, que volvió a demostrar en Atenas su carácter competitivo. "Este equipo nunca da una pelota por perdida. Ya sueña con volver a ser campeón", aseguró, comparando esa mentalidad con la de Rafa Nadal. Villa cerró su reflexión con una advertencia directa al futbolista brasileño, al que considera cada vez menos determinante en el proyecto madridista: "El brasileño ha dejado de ser imprescindible en un Madrid que ha recuperado su religión: creer hasta el último suspiro". Y terminó con una pregunta que resume su opinión sobre el futuro del extremo: "Vinicius debe decidir si quiere volar con él".

articles.title: Los cuatro problemas del Real Madrid de Mourinho
articles.standfirst: José Luis Sánchez cree que cuando acabe el castigo al brasileño, Mourinho le dejará en el banquillo viendo los últimos partidos del equipo
articles.summary: José Luis Sánchez cree que cuando acabe el castigo al brasileño, Mourinho le dejará en el banquillo viendo los últimos partidos del equipo
articles.body: Látigo Serrano analizó durante una de sus intervenciones en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, las carencias del conjunto blanco y fue especialmente crítico con el rendimiento de Vinicius, cuya situación considera uno de los grandes problemas que debe resolver el equipo. "Sin Tchouaméni el equipo pierde equilibrio; sin Güler el equipo pierde fútbol; con Vinicius en el campo atacan con diez y defienden con nueve", aseguró Serrano, que también señaló las dificultades para encajar a las grandes estrellas madridistas en un mismo once. En este sentido, el periodista cuestionó la compatibilidad de tres de los futbolistas más importantes de la plantilla: "Vinicius, Bellingham y Mbappé no pueden jugar juntos porque tienden a ocupar el mismo espacio o un espacio similar en el campo". La reflexión más contundente de Látigo Serrano llegó al analizar qué debe hacer el Real Madrid con Vinicius. Para el periodista, el bajo rendimiento del brasileño no admite demasiadas dudas: "El diagnóstico de Vinicius es que no está para jugar en el Real Madrid ahora mismo". Sin embargo, considera que la verdadera dificultad está en encontrar una solución a su situación. "Y el problema no es el diagnóstico, es el tratamiento. ¿Qué haces con Vinicius? ¿Le sientas? No puedes, no puedes tener a un jugador que gana 25 millones de euros en el banquillo aunque lo merezca", explicó. Serrano comparó además el trato recibido por el brasileño con el de Diomande, recordando las diferencias en sus respectivas suplencias: "Diomande estuvo cinco partidos como suplente porque era nuevo. Vinicius ha estado solo un partido de suplente". El periodista cerró su análisis con una advertencia sobre las consecuencias que podría tener para el Real Madrid dejar al brasileño fuera del once de manera continuada: "Si está cinco partidos seguidos como suplente, que es lo que merece, el Madrid tiene un problema gordísimo".

articles.title: Manchester United manager latest: No interim planned should club decide to sack Michael Carrick
articles.summary: Manchester United are set to avoid appointing an interim manager should they decide to sack Michael Carrick; Carrick's future is under increasing pressure after winning just one of his last 10 games in charge; Carrick still holds support within the club's hierarchy
articles.body:
There is still support for Carrick among the United hierarchy, and a lingering concern that changing the head coach won't necessarily change the team's fortunes.

The Champions League victory over Roma on Tuesday night has provided some respite, and boosted belief in the changing room and the boardroom. It was their first win in 10 matches in all competitions.

However, there is a realisation that one win on its own isn't enough to turn a season around. United remain 17th in the Premier League, only outside the relegation places on goal difference. And the nature of the victory against Roma was chaotic.

Whilst the character of the team to come back from 2-0 down suggests the players are still behind Carrick, it took a re-taken Bruno Fernandes penalty to turn the tide, and United's bosses still have doubts about the team's direction and lack of consistency.

Carrick was given the top job on a two-year basis in May, after a brilliant record as interim United head coach that secured Champions League football. There was a clamour from United fans for their former midfielder to be given the role substantively.

Nevertheless, United's bosses were determined to carry out a period of due diligence when they did speak to other candidates before appointing Carrick. And it's thought United wouldn't want to repeat that process of having an interim head coach, as they try to take a longer-term strategy over their most important football role.

Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada, who run United's football operations, are still considering other options, should they feel they need to make a change. And with the international break next week offering a chance to take a breath and reassess, there is a feeling that Super Sunday's game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford is a key one for Carrick's future.

The fact that Sunday's opponents have now announced they are close to agreeing a new long-term contract with Unai Emery - and a new long-term strategy with the Spaniard and his staff at the heart of the club's planning - comes as a blow to Manchester United.

Emery was high up on United's list of potential future targets, with admiration for the way he has twice secured Champions League football and also the club's first European trophy in over four decades, with victory in the Europa League in May. However, there has always been a realisation that it would be difficult - and expensive - to try to get Emery out of Villa Park, especially mid-season, with Villa's owners adamant he is going nowhere.

As a result, United's bosses have remained open-minded about other potential candidates, with Julian Nagelsmann , Fabian Hurzeler and Eddie Howe prominent in their thinking.

So far, United have not spoken directly to any other coach, with the feeling that there is no current vacancy. The preferred option on all sides is that results improve, and Carrick remains in charge of the team.

articles.title: England’s Harry Kane extends Bayern Munich contract until 2029
articles.summary: ‘I love the club, the fans and the city,’ says the Ballon d’Or ‌winner after extending his stay with German champions.
articles.body:
Ballon d’Or ‌winner Harry Kane has signed a contract extension with Bayern Munich until June ⁠2029, the ⁠Bundesliga club has announced.

“I feel right at home at FC Bayern,” Kane said in a statement announcing his extention with Bayern Munich on Thursday.

The England captain joined Bayern from Tottenham Hotspur in 2023 and has since helped the German side win two Bundesliga titles, ⁠the German Cup and two German Super Cups.

The 33-year-old striker has scored 156 goals in 161 appearances in all competitions for Bayern and capped his prolific spell in Munich ⁠by winning the Ballon d’Or last week .

He was the first Englishman to win the prestigious award since Michael Owen in 2001.

“I love the club, the fans and the city of Munich. We have a fantastic ‌team and, in Vincent Kompany, a fantastic manager,” the star forward went on to add.

“It makes me very proud to be part of this club. My whole family is very happy here. I was keen to stay. I’m now looking forward to the future and I want to win many more titles with this great club.”

Kane has frequently been linked with a move back to England, where he remains 47 goals shy of Alan Shearer’s Premier League record ⁠of 260 goals.

However, the striker said in August that the Premier ⁠League no longer holds the same appeal for him as he is focused on his career in Germany.

“Since joining us in 2023, he has achieved extraordinary things with his goals, his influence on the game and ⁠as a role model both on and off the pitch,” Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen said.

“His contract extension is a commitment to FC ⁠Bayern and to a story that is far from ⁠over.”

Bayern did not disclose financial details of the agreement. However, German media reported that the extension is the most lucrative contract in the club’s history and part of a long-term commitment to the England captain.

Kane has finished as ‌the Bundesliga’s top scorer in each of his seasons with Bayern and was named Germany’s Footballer of the Year in 2026.

He has also won the European Golden Shoe twice, awarded ‌to ‌Europe’s leading league goalscorer, and captained England to a third-place finish at this year’s World Cup.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo se retira de la selección de Portugal
articles.standfirst: El astro luso anuncia su adiós al combinado luso
articles.summary: El astro luso anuncia su adiós al combinado luso
articles.body: En un emotivo vídeo publicado en sus redes sociales, el astro portugués ha leído una extensa carta en la que pone fin a su trayectoria a la selección lusa. Tras un tiempo de reflexión después de la última ventana de selecciones, Cristiano Ronaldo cuelga el brazalete de la selección. Para los portugueses: ha llegado el día de devolver la camiseta siete de la selección de todos nosotros. Nunca lo sentí exclusivamente mío, pero durante 23 años tuve el privilegio y la responsabilidad de vestirla, de defenderlo y llevarlo conmigo a estadios de todo el mundo. Hoy llego la hora de entregarlo al futuro. No fue una decisión fácil, porque hay decisiones que no se toman sólo con la cabeza, también se toman con el corazón. Finaliza un viaje que comenzó en Agosto de 2003 y cambió mi vida para siempre. Cuando miro atrás y pienso en todo que viví en la selección, no solo veo partidos, goles, récords o trofeos. Veo millones de portugueses que nunca conocí en persona, pero que formaron parte de mi vida. Porque al final de todo, el fútbol es mucho más grande que un juego. El fútbol es la gente. A lo largo de mi carrera en la selección, traté de superar mis límites. Quería ganar, quería ser el mejor, Quería hacer historia. Siempre he sido exigente conmigo mismo, siempre quise más, siempre creí que podíamos llegar más lejos y di todo lo que tenía por esta camiseta. Hubo tardes y noches perfectas, hubo victorias que nunca olvidaré, hubo derrotas que aún hoy existen en mi memoria. Me cuesta recordarlo. Yo también fallé, también sufrí. Hubo momentos en los que no pude darle a los portugueses lo que tanto quería, pero nunca me rendí y, sobre todo, nunca dejé de sentirme orgulloso de representar a Portugal. A lo largo de estos años, aprendí cosas muy simples. Los goles pasan, las copas se quedan en los museos, los récords terminan batiéndose, pero hay algo que el tiempo nunca puede borrar: el lugar que ocupamos en el corazón de personas. Si alguna vez te hice feliz, si alguna vez un gol mío te hizo abrazar a alguien, olvidar una preocupación... Todo valió la pena. Porque ser portugués también es esto. Sufrimos juntos, nos levantamos juntos. Volvemos a creer. Portugal siempre necesitará gente joven que sueñe, jugadores que nunca se rinden, nuevas generaciones que creen que es posible llegar a donde nadie ha llegado. Porque un país que sigue creando nuevos héroes es un país que nunca va a dejar de creer en sí mismo. A mi compañeros: me quiero ir una palabra especial. Gracias por cada carrera, por cada abrazo, por cada discusión, por cada silencio antes de entrar al campo, cada victoria la celebramos juntos y por cada derrota que nos hizo más fuertes. Tuve el privilegio de ser tu capitán, pero ningún capitán camina solo y eres parte de mi historia. A todos los entrenadores, directivos, médicos, fisioterapeutas, guardarropas, empleados y tanta gente que han trabajado conmigo a lo largo de los años, gracias. Muchos de ustedes nunca han aparecido en fotografías, pero sin vosotros ninguna de estas fotografías hubiera sido posible. A mi familia, gracias por compartir este sueño conmigo. Gracias por entender las ausencias, los sacrificios y los momentos en los que el equipo tuvo que ocupar un espacio que también os pertenecía. Si llegué hasta aquí fue porque siempre estuvimos dispuestos. Y a los portugueses, a todos, a los portugueses repartidos por el mundo: quiero deciros una última cosa. Hay un imagen que llevaré siempre conmigo, el momento en el que comienza el himno nacional. Miro a mi alrededor, veo a mi compañeros, veo las gradas, veo niños, madres, padres y abuelos, veo portugueses que vinieron de tan lejos sólo para estar allí. Y durante esos minutos dejamos de ser diferentes. No hay clubes, no hay colores, no hay clases, no hay profesiones, no hay opiniones. Hay solo una pasión. Portugal: Este es el sentimiento que llevaré conmigo, por el resto de mi vida. Hoy termina mi paseo por el campo con la selección nacional. Salgo de pie, con orgullo por el camino que recorrí y con el conocimiento de que lo di todo. Pero nunca dejaré de ser uno de ustedes. Seguiré sufriendo, vibrando y celebrando cada victoria portuguesa contigo. Pasé mi vida trabajando para ser el mejor jugador del mundo. Hoy me doy cuenta de que la mayor victoria fue haberla merecido. Representar al mejor país del mundo. Gracias por estos 23 años. Gracias por creer en mí. Gracias por permitirme vivir una sueño que empezó cuando yo era apenas un niño, en el bosque, corriendo detrás de una pelota. La camisa 7 se queda. El orgullo de haberla vestido será mío para siempre. Portugal siempre estará en mí. Hasta siempre. Cristiano Ronaldo. Hay futbolistas que marcan una época y otros que cambian para siempre la historia de una selección. Cristiano Ronaldo pertenece a la segunda categoría. Cuando debutó con Portugal en 2003, el combinado luso seguía buscando su primer gran título. Más de dos décadas después, se marcha dejando una herencia irrepetible: tres trofeos internacionales, 146 goles y un legado que transformó para siempre la dimensión competitiva de su país. La imagen que mejor resume su trayectoria llegó en la noche del 10 de julio de 2016. Aquel día, en el Stade de France, Portugal conquistó la primera Eurocopa de su historia tras derrotar a Francia. Cristiano sufrió una lesión que le obligó a abandonar el terreno de juego, pero acabó ejerciendo casi como un seleccionador más desde la banda durante una prórroga que culminó con el histórico gol de Eder. Fue el primer gran título de una generación que encontró en su capitán el liderazgo necesario para dar el salto definitivo. Tres años después, el astro portugués volvió a levantar un trofeo con la selección al conquistar la primera edición de la UEFA Nations League. Antes de la final ante Países Bajos, Cristiano ya había dejado su sello con un espectacular triplete frente a Suiza que metió a Portugal en el partido por el título. Su colección de éxitos internacionales se completó con una segunda Nations League, conquistada en 2025, demostrando que seguía siendo competitivo incluso después de cumplir los 40 años. Pero reducir la trayectoria de Cristiano a los títulos sería quedarse corto. Su impacto se mide también en cifras que parecen destinadas a permanecer durante décadas. Nadie ha marcado más goles con una selección nacional. Nadie ha vestido más veces la camiseta portuguesa. Nadie ha llevado tan lejos la ambición de un país que pasó de ser una selección talentosa a convertirse en una potencia capaz de competir por cualquier torneo. Entre generaciones doradas, finales perdidas y noches históricas, Cristiano construyó una carrera internacional que trasciende los trofeos. Portugal ya tenía héroes antes de él. Lo que no tenía era una leyenda capaz de convertir la victoria en costumbre. Y eso, durante más de 20 años, llevó su nombre: Cristiano Ronaldo.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from international soccer after a record-breaking career with Portugal
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international soccer after a record-breaking career with Portugal.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international soccer after a record-breaking career with Portugal. The 41-year-old broke the news on Thursday in a long video where he read a letter to his supporters. “The day has come for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our national team,” he said, referring to his iconic shirt number. “I never thought it belonged to me alone. But for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it.” Ronaldo played a record 234 times for his country, scoring a record 146 international goals. No man has scored more or made more appearances for his nation. The highlight of his international career came in 2016 when he lifted the European Championship trophy for his country. He also helped Portugal to victory in the UEFA Nations League in 2019 and 2025. Public fallout Despite all his success, though, his relationship with the national team has slowly soured over the last few years – much in part due to his declining performances on the field. Despite age clearly catching up with him, Ronaldo continued starting despite his impact waning and fans began to grow frustrated. After this summer’s World Cup in North America, the striker then clashed with new head coach Jorge Jesus and stormed out of a national team training camp last month. Ronaldo had apologized, though, and it appeared that he’d continue his career for the national team. His announcement comes shortly after rival Lionel Messi also retired from playing international soccer with Argentina. Despite the unceremonious ending, no one can doubt the impact Ronaldo has had on Portuguese soccer. For many, he is the greatest player the country has ever produced and he powered the team to its first-ever major silverware. “It was not an easy decision, because there are decisions that are not made only with the head. ​They are also made with the heart,” Ronaldo said in his video, titled “Portugal will ​always ⁠be a part of me.” “If I ever made you happy, if one ‌of ⁠my goals ever made you hug someone, forget a worry or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it.” What next? Ronaldo’s announcement comes ahead of the international break later this month, when the Seleção is set to play Denmark and Wales in the UEFA Nations League. The Portuguese Football Federation said in a statement Thursday that it “refuses to let this farewell take place without due tribute,” as it prepares to announce its squad for the upcoming fixtures. “It is our firm and immense desire to organize, plan, participate, and actively collaborate in what will always be a fitting tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo’s immense career, in which fans and the country can applaud and celebrate, once again, the player who has given us so much,” it said. The superstar is not retiring completely, though. He still plays for Saudi Arabian side Al-Nassr FC where he is closing in on scoring 1,000 career goals – he’s currently on 985. articles.title: Sky Sports and Sir Gareth Southgate’s 1071 Media partner to launch new football content
articles.summary: Partnership will work on three social-first shows, The Football Dugout, The Football Data Room, and The Football Boardcast; The shows will explore different sides of the modern game, from business to tactical analysis and the growing influence of data and technology
articles.body:
The partnership will see Sky Sports integrate their expertise and resources into three social-first shows, including two new formats, with Sky Media representing all commercially. The shows will explore different sides of the modern game; from the business and decision-making behind football's biggest stories, to technical and tactical analysis, and the growing influence of data and technology.

The partnership brings together two new formats alongside 1071 Media's existing football property, The Football Boardroom (TFB), which has seen significant growth and engagement since its launch earlier this year. As part of the new partnership with Sky, the show will be renamed The Football Boardcast (TFB) and will continue to be published on its existing YouTube and audio channels.

The Football Dugout - a new weekly podcast and YouTube show co-hosted by Sky Sports football presenter, Mark Chapman, and former England defender, Conor Coady, who is currently coaching with England U21s. The show will feature conversations with managers, players, coaches and sporting directors, exploring the technical and tactical side of the game. Recorded in The Pod, a mobile podcasting studio designed to travel to wherever the conversation is happening, the show will launch on a new YouTube channel and will be available on all major audio platforms.

The Football Data Room - a new video analysis and data-led show launching on the Sky Sports Premier League YouTube channel, focused on the numbers and trends driving modern football. Hosted by Sky Sports Saturday Social presenter, Joe Thomlinson, alongside football analysts, "Statman Dave" and Jamie Osman, formerly of West Ham United and Ipswich Town, the show combines data with expert insight. Up to three 20-minute episodes will be released each week, spanning match reviews, previews, and opinion-led discussion.

The Football Boardcast - hosted by highly respected former top executive at Liverpool, Chelsea and Aston Villa, Christian Purslow, and award-winning football journalist, Henry Winter, the show takes fans inside the money, power, and politics that shape the modern game. Weekly episodes will continue on The Football Boardcast's existing YouTube and audio channels, now represented by Sky Media.

The new shows will complement Sky Sports' existing social content and further expand its offering for digital audiences. Earlier this year, Sky Sports surpassed one billion engagements across its social platforms and now has more than 130 million aggregated subscribers across its social channels.

CEO, Sky Sports UK & Ireland, Jonathan Licht , said: "As the home of sport for fans across the UK & Ireland, this partnership reflects our ambition to provide more choice and entertainment beyond the live action and bring different voices, fresh perspectives and expanded insight into the game.

"We have years of expertise, an unmatched passion for sport and huge reach. Combining that with 1071 Media's creativity and insight, we can create compelling new football content and take it to fans wherever and however they choose to engage with the game."

Sir Gareth Southgate , 1071 Media co-founder, said: "It has always been 1071 Media's intention to combine exciting new concepts with the leading thinkers in sport to educate, inform and entertain fans. With the launch of three football shows covering the boardroom, the boot room and the data room, we hope fans gain greater insight into the business, the tactics, and the analysis to explain how the game really works. We couldn't ask for a better partner than Sky Sports, who have set the standard in broadcasting for decades. Together, we can bring supporters everywhere closer to the conversations that shape football, with expert voices and a fresh perspective on the sport they love."

Sky Sports is the home of domestic football, with more than 1,500 live games this season across the Premier League, EFL, SPFL, and WSL. From the 2027/28 season, Sky Sports will also show every match from the UEFA Europa League and UEFA Conference League, frequently giving customers access to live football seven days a week.

articles.title: Balaídos: Donde se consolidó la permanencia y el Castrismo
articles.standfirst: El Levante consiguió la temporada pasada un triunfo ante el Celta un triunfo vital para quedarse en Primera
articles.summary: El Levante consiguió la temporada pasada un triunfo ante el Celta un triunfo vital para quedarse en Primera
articles.body: El estadio de Balaidos fue donde terminó de forjarse el Castrismo y creer firmemente en la permanencia el pasado curso. El Levante, que llevó al tramo final con un pie en la zona roja y otro en la permanencia, certificó prácticamente su salvación con una victoria en el feudo celeste. Después de una victoria en el Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán, en el día de su debut en el banquillo granota, por un contundente cero a tres, los valencianos no volvieron a sumar de tres hasta cuatro meses más tarde. En la jornada 36 del campeonato nacional de liga en Primera División. Tras pasar por el Santiago Bernabéu, San Mamés, Camp Nou, Vallecas, Anoeta, Cornellá- El Prat y La Cerámica; la renta de triunfos en casa, un total de seis, seguir en la máxima categoría del fútbol español dependía de un triunfo lejos del barrio de Orriols. Y llegó en la penúltima salida del año. Con el Celta jugándose entrar en las posiciones europeas, los azulgranas saltaron al campo con la ambición de llevarse un empate, como mínimo. Aunque la historia fue bien distinta. A pesar de recibir un gol en los primeros minutos, tras el tanto de Jutglà, el Levante no perdió la esperanza y Arriaga consiguió empatar el choque antes del descanso. De nuevo Jutglà puso por delante al equipo entrenado por Giraldez y a partir de aquí, es historia viva de Luís Castro. El equipo perdió el miedo y consiguió una remontada clave para consolidar su candidatura para mantenerse en Primera. Dela empató el envite con un impresionante derechazo desde más de treinta metros que acabó en la escuadra de la portería de Iván Villar y cinco minutos más tarde, Brugué aprovechó un mal cálculo de Javi Rueda en el despeje de un córner del equipo valenciano, y anotó el tercer y definitivo gol de la remontada.

articles.title: García Plaza se acuerda de Owono: "No hagamos dos víctimas"
articles.standfirst: El técnico, muy afectado tras la muerte de Jesús de Miguel: "No se tendría que jugar"
articles.summary: El técnico, muy afectado tras la muerte de Jesús de Miguel: "No se tendría que jugar"
articles.body: Luis García Plaza ha comparecido ante los medios en la previa del partido de mañana (21.00 horas) frente al Alavés. No ha sido un comienzo de rueda de prensa fácil para el entrenador del Sevilla. "Nos toca hacer de portavoz del club aunque a veces no es nuestra función, pero como somos los que hablamos tantas veces a lo largo de una semana, mandar en mi nombre, de toda la plantilla y del club, aunque lo ha hecho en las redes sociales, todo nuestro apoyo, el más sentido pésame a toda la familia de Jesús de Miguel, a todos sus amigos, a toda la gente del fútbol. Es una auténtica desgracia lo que ha pasado y poco más. Las palabras sobran. Estar con ellos e intentar ayudar en todo lo que podamos dentro de nuestra posición. Nada más. Descanse en paz", dijo el madrileño antes de atender a las preguntas de los periodistas. "Para la sociedad española son días complicados, para todo el conjunto del país. El accidente de tren, que fue muy doloroso para muchas familias, y ahora es algo que nos toca a los profesionales del fútbol que es la muerte de un jugador en el terreno de juego y no es fácil, pero tienes que seguir. A mí me toca algo personalmente por Owono, que es una desgracia lo que le ha pasado. Es un chaval, lo tengo que decir, espectacular, un chaval que no podemos comparar lo de Jesús, no podemos hacer dos víctimas, ya ha habido una y seguro que estará en un infierno, aunque nada comparable y siempre por detrás de lo de Jesús", comentaba. García Plaza tuvo a sus órdenes al guardameta del Andorra cuando coincidieron en el Alavés. Y añadía: "Es una desgracia, son momentos complicados, pero aquí estáis los periodistas, estamos todos haciendo nuestro trabajo y siguiendo con la vida. No hay más. Una opinión de Luis García Plaza es que no se tendría que jugar, hablo de mí personalmente, igual que no se tuvo que jugar la Copa del Rey, igual que lo dije el año pasado durante la DANA, no se tiene que jugar en estos momentos. Si hay que jugar lo haremos, son tres puntos importantísimos igual que pasó entonces con el Alavés y ganamos 1-0. Mañana a tope, a jugar, a competir y a intentar ganar". Para finalizar la rueda de prensa dejó una reflexión: "Mañana, como haya un balón largo nuestro, si va a salir o no Sivera, o si hay un balón para Odysseas... Está muy reciente. Como se dé una jugada igual... ¿qué le digo a mi portero? Por eso digo lo de dejar pasar un poco de tiempo. Es mi sensación. Intentaremos competir pero tiene que servir como reflexión, que pongamos todos los medios para estar lo más preparados posibles para cualquier cosa que pueda pasar con un jugador, un aficionado... En un balón dividido, mañana, los jugadores del Alavés y del Sevilla lo van a tener aquí (señalándose la cabeza) porque está muy reciente".
