articles.title: Man Utd: Paul Merson says Michael Carrick needs Bruno Fernandes on side and Matheus Cunha to be consistent
articles.summary: Paul Merson explains why Bruno Fernandes must remain in Manchester United’s team, challenges Matheus Cunha to find consistency and warns Michael Carrick that Sunday’s clash with Aston Villa, live on Sky Sports, will be a major test after the Roma comeback.
articles.body:
United showed plenty of character to recover from two goals down in the Champions League on Tuesday, earning their first win in 10 games, but Merson believes the result should not disguise the problems that remain under Carrick.

Merson also questioned whether United can carry that momentum into Sunday's Premier League clash with Aston Villa, live on Sky Sports.

"I think Bruno Fernandes has to play for Manchester United. He's their best player, and when you're going through a difficult period, you need your best players on the pitch.

"It takes a lot to miss a penalty, then have the courage to step up and take it again. The pressure was severely on him, so fair play to him.

"I know he was left out against Roma, but I don't think you can keep leaving him out. Even if he's not playing particularly well, he still gets into Manchester United's team. They haven't got a player better than him.

"You couldn't keep chopping your nose off to spite your face. You need him on side.

"Brian Clough always used to say that when times are hard, go back to putting your best team on the pitch. Put it in your drawer, and when things aren't going well, go back to that team.

"That's what United need to do. Bruno has to be in it. As long as he plays well, they will always have a chance of winning.

"But I still think they need to become much more of a 90-minute team. They were very good against Chelsea in the first half on Saturday, and they had good spells in the second half against Roma, but you aren't going to win too many football matches playing like that.

"You need 70 or 75 minutes of good football, not 10 minutes here and 15 minutes there."

Cunha can't be a nine one week and a four the next

"Matheus Cunha is a passionate player, and I like that about him, but I said something in my column the other day about his performances. He's a nine or a four.

"At Wolves, he could be a nine one week and they would win a football match. The following week he might be a four and they wouldn't win. That's the nature of being at a club fighting towards the bottom of the table.

"But this is Manchester United. When you play for a club of that size, you've got to be a seven or a seven-and-a-half every week. You can be an eight, you can have a nine, but you can't be a nine one week and a four the next.

"That's the difference when you go to a big football club. These teams need to win week in, week out. They can't afford to rely on one outstanding performance every few weeks.

"Cunha might not have been used to those expectations at Wolves, but that's what comes with playing for Manchester United.

"Look at Carlos Baleba. He's only just arrived, and it was a shame to see him pull his hamstring. But he'll be sitting there thinking, 'when I was at Brighton and we lost, nobody said a word. Now I'm at Manchester United, losing against one of the top teams, and we're getting destroyed after the game'.

"That's the environment you're playing in. You're at one of the biggest football clubs in the world, and the standards have to reflect that."

Roma comeback showed bottle - but United rode their luck

"You've got to live in the moment, and it was an amazing comeback from Manchester United.

"At 2-0 down, given the run they've been on, it would have been difficult to get those players back out on the pitch for the second half. So I give them a lot of credit for that.

"They showed a lot of bottle but they rode their luck.

"Bruno gets the opportunity to retake his penalty. If they don't get that decision, do they get back into the game? Roma then make a mistake at the back, miskicking the ball. You shouldn't be doing that at this level.

"And for the winning goal, I don't really see a goalkeeper in the Premier League letting that one in at the near post.

"So, yes, credit where credit is due. It was a brilliant comeback and it could be the result that turns their season around. But I don't think you can look at that performance and say everything has suddenly changed.

"I feel sorry for Michael Carrick. I don't think it's him; I think it's the players."

Villa will provide a reality check on Sunday

"I don't see the Roma result as a turnaround for Manchester United. I think it's a start, but if I'm being honest, I don't see them getting anything from Aston Villa on Sunday.

"Villa weren't great against Barcelona, but they're playing a much better standard of football at the moment.

"Roma covered over the cracks, in my opinion. It's not like they absolutely destroyed Roma. They got back into it by bad luck.

"I'm more interested in what happens this weekend from Manchester United."

Manchester United host Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday, live on Sky Sports, with kick-off at 4.30pm.

articles.title: 'There is only one passion: PORTUGAL': Cristiano Ronaldo bids emotional farewell to national team; Read full speech
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has officially brought the curtain down on his illustrious international career, announcing his retirement from Portugal duty after 23
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has officially brought the curtain down on his illustrious international career, announcing his retirement from Portugal duty after 23 years, six World Cup appearances and a record-breaking haul of 146 goals in 234 matches.The five-time Ballon d'Or winner made the announcement on Thursday through an emotional video message addressed to the Portuguese people, confirming that his journey with the national team had reached its end. However, the 41-year-old is not retiring from professional football and is expected to continue playing for Saudi Arabian club Al-Nassr until the end of the current season.Ronaldo's international career began in August 2003, before Euro 2004, and saw him become one of the most influential figures in Portuguese football history. He captained the country to its maiden major international trophy at Euro 2016 and subsequently lifted the inaugural UEFA Nations League title in 2019.He also holds the men's all-time international scoring record with 146 goals, having represented Portugal in six editions of the FIFA World Cup. Ronaldo is currently pursuing the remarkable milestone of 1,000 career goals, with his tally standing at 985.Ronaldo's Portugal farewell follows tense spell with coach Jorge JesusThe announcement comes after a difficult period involving Portugal coach Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo's last appearance for the national side came on September 24, when Portugal registered a 1-0 home victory over Wales in the Nations League.Jesus subsequently left the veteran forward on the bench for the following match and indicated that he did not intend to start him in the next fixture either. Ronaldo then decided to leave the national team's training camp. Although Jesus later said the forward would be welcome back and that the decision to return rested with him, Ronaldo has now brought his international career to an end.His farewell comes shortly after long-time rival Lionel Messi brought his international career with Argentina to a close last month following a much-anticipated farewell appearance.The Portuguese Football Federation paid tribute to Ronaldo, expressing "deep gratitude and immense admiration" for his contribution to the country.In his farewell message, Ronaldo spoke about the sacrifices, victories, defeats and emotional connections that defined his 23-year journey. He also thanked his teammates, coaches, support staff and family, while reflecting on what representing Portugal meant to him.One passage particularly captured the emotion of his farewell, with Ronaldo declaring: "There is only one passion: PORTUGAL."He signed off by promising to continue supporting the national side, adding that he would keep celebrating every Portuguese victory with his trademark "Siuuu!"Read full text of Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement announcement speech"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number 7 shirt of our national team. I never felt it belonged to me alone. But for 23 years, I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it, and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world. Today, the time has come to pass it on to the future.It was not an easy decision. Because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart. A journey that began in August 2003, and changed my life forever, has come to an end. When I look back at everything I experienced with the national team, I don't just see matches, goals, records, or trophies. I see people. I see Portuguese people living abroad, who, for ninety minutes, felt a little closer to home. I see millions of Portuguese people I have never met, but who became part of my life. Because, at the end of the day, football is so much bigger than a game. Football is about people.Throughout my entire career with the national team, I always pushed myself beyond my limits. I wanted to win. I wanted to be better. I wanted to make history. I always demanded the most of myself. I always wanted more. I always believed we could go further. And I gave everything I had for this shirt. There were perfect afternoons and nights. There were victories I will never forget. There were defeats that still hurt to remember. I made mistakes. I suffered. There were also moments when I couldn't give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted. But I never gave up. And above all, I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.Over the years, I learned a few very simple things: goals fade. Trophies end up in museums. Records are eventually broken. But there is something that time can never erase: the place we hold in people's hearts. If I ever made you happy, if one of my goals ever made you embrace someone, forget a worry, or feel proud of our country, then it was all worth it. Because being Portuguese is also about this. We suffer together. We rise together. We believe again.Portugal will always need young people who dare to dream. Players who never give up. New generations who believe it is possible to go where no one has gone before. Because a country that keeps creating new heroes is a country that never stops believing in itself.To my teammates, I want to say something special. Thank you for every run. For every embrace. For every argument. For every silence before stepping onto the pitch. For every victory we celebrated together, and for every defeat that made us stronger. I had the privilege of being your captain, but no captain walks alone. And you will always be part of my story. To all the coaches, directors, doctors, physiotherapists, kit managers, staff members, and so many others who worked alongside me throughout these years, thank you. Many of you never appeared in the photographs. But without you, none of these photographs would never been possible.To my family.. Thank you for sharing this dream with me. Thank you for understanding the absences, the sacrifices, and the moments when the national team had to take up a space in my life that also belonged to you. If I came this far, it was because we always hand in hand.And to the people of Portugal...To every Portuguese person, wherever you are in the world, there is one last thing I want to tell you. There is an image I will carry with me forever. The moment our national anthem begins. I look around. I see my teammates. I see the stands. I see children, mothers, fathers and grandparents. I see Portuguese people who have travelled so far just to be there. And for those few minutes, all our differences disappear. There are no clubs. There are no colours. There are no classes. There are no professions. There are no opinions.There is only one passion: PORTUGAL. That is the feeling I will carry with me for the rest of my life.Today, my journey on the pitch with the national team comes to an end. I leave with my head held high. Proud of the path I have taken, and knowing that I gave everything I had for Portugal. But I will never stop being one of you. I will keep suffering, cheering, and celebrating every Portuguese victory with a Siuuuuu!I spent my life working to be the best player in the world. Today, I realise that my greatest victory was earning the honour to representing the best country in the world.Thank you for these 23 years. Thank you for believing in me. Thank you for allowing me to live a dream that began when I was just a little boy, in Madeira, running after a football.The number 7 shirt will remain. The pride of having worn it will be mine forever. Portugal will always be a part of me. Farewell, until we meet again. Cristiano Ronaldo"Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. The Heisman Trophy contender is out with an ankle injury. He is second in the FBS in receptions and third in receiving yards.

Toney had 34 receptions just in the last three weeks for the high-powered Miami offense. No one else inside the Miami offense has more than 28 receptions.

Cooper Barkate, Daylyn Upshaw and Elija Lofton are the other Hurricanes with 20+ receptions this season. All of them will have elevated roles in the passing game moving forward.

While the passing attack will be under a microscope, the Mark Fletcher Jr.-led rushing attack will be the key to Miami winning. Fletcher has a touchdown in all but one game this season, but he hasn't been utilized as much as last season because of the dynamic passing attack.

Miami can win this game by controlling the time of possession and wearing down the Notre Dame defense through Fletcher.

Notre Dame absolutely needs to play from ahead at home so that the Miami passing attack has to win the game for the ACC side.

The Fighting Irish have to treat Saturday like an elimination game because they are 11th in the CFB Playoff rankings. A second loss will knock the Irish out of contention due to the lack of high-quality opponents left on their schedule.

Look for Jaden Greathouse and Jordan Faison, the Irish's two veteran wide outs, to play huge roles on Saturday. The duo combined for 14 receptions and 189 receiving yards in the loss to BYU.

The Miami defense conceded over 30 points in two of its last three games. C.J. Carr has the opportunity to take advantage of a vulnerable defense and win the game through the air.

Miami can keep the game close without Toney, but it needs one of its wide receivers to make a big play or two, regardless of if Fletcher succeeds on the ground or not.

The Hurricanes can suffer a loss and still remain in the playoff field. They should win their final three regular-season games, all of which are at home against unranked ACC teams.

The game simply means more to Notre Dame.

The Irish should win, but the spread is a bit heavy now that Toney is out. The Hurricanes likely won't get blown out, so it's worth taking them with the 7.5.

Utah comes into the Holy War with the better ranking than BYU, but the Cougars have had the upper hand in the rivalry lately.

BYU won three games in a row against its in-state rival. It won twice at home and once in Salt Lake City during that stretch.

Utah won nine straight games in the rivalry before BYU took over as the dominant side.

The game is more consequential for BYU because it has one loss from an upset on the road against the UCF Knights. At No. 9, there's a good chance BYU misses the 12-team playoff with two losses.

Utah is sitting at No. 3 with one of the final undefeated records in the FBS.

The Cougars received a huge boost with LJ Martin's injury news. The star running back is questionable, per ESPN's Pete Thamel. He won't be at 100 percent, but just having him on the field might help BYU's offense.

The BYU-Utah game hasn't produced a ton of offensive fireworks in recent years. The last four games have had 45 points or fewer.

The safest bet is to rely on both defenses to show up with an extra bit of intensity for the early kickoff in Utah. Both teams give up less than 20 points per game.

Utah has the home-field advantage, which might be the difference-maker in such a tight game, but the bigger guarantee is the lack of points and explosive big plays.

Georgia likely has revenge on its mind as it enters Oxford this weekend.

The Bulldogs were knocked out of the CFB Playoff last season by Trinidad Chambliss and Ole Miss. Chambliss threw for 362 yards and led Ole Miss to 39 points against the normally reliable UGA defense.

Georgia hasn't given up more than 20 points in a victory this season and it appeared to get back on track with its 27-8 win over the Florida Gators last week in Atlanta.

UGA might be the most reliable national title contender now that Miami will be without Toney for a while.

Kirby Smart's team has a strong defense and a steady hand at quarterback in Gunner Stockton, who has a 71.8 completion percentage and only turned the ball over four times.

Chambliss is arguably the best quarterback in the FBS right now, but Ole Miss is 2-2 against ranked teams in 2026.

Georgia is the toughest matchup the Rebels will face and the Bulldogs likely won't let Chambliss throw the ball all over the yard again.

Saturday could be a statement game for the Bulldogs to assert their dominance at the top of the SEC and atop the list of CFB Playoff contenders.

articles.title: Can Norway success open doors in Laura Kaminski's coaching career?
articles.summary: English manager Laura Kaminski has won the Norwegian league and cup double - so will that open doors in her coaching career?
articles.body:
When English manager Laura Kaminski was approached to become the head coach of Norwegian club SK Brann in January, she could not turn it down.

She jumped at the opportunity to move abroad and develop her coaching skills and is even competing for a place in the Europa Cup quarter-finals next Wednesday.

It was a decision that paid off as 10 months later, she is celebrating a Norwegian league and cup double after a dream debut season.

"My time in the city [of Bergen] has been brilliant," the 38-year-old told BBC Sport.

"I can't go to the supermarket at the minute because so many people are stopping me to wish me congratulations, which is so nice.

"I'm over the moon and it was nice to get the title done before the last game so we can relax. I thought it was going to go right to the wire.

"It's been a competitive year. I've enjoyed every minute. We had a great night with all our fans, who were waiting for us to return from Oslo."

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

65 flights and games in the Arctic Circle

Kaminski described it as a "hectic" year as she moved from London to Norway and away from her family to take on the Brann job.

The Englishwoman had spent over a year at Crystal Palace, where she led them to promotion to the Women's Super League in 2024.

She was sacked in February 2025 after a tough WSL season as Palace struggled to compete with better financially-backed clubs.

However, she is regarded as one of the country's brightest female managers and has added to her CV with her experiences in Norway.

"I've learned a lot. It's been chaotic - I counted that I have taken 65 flights in 11 months - so it's been exhausting, but what an experience!" added Kaminski.

"To go all the way up to the Arctic Circle and play away [games] in freezing cold conditions with horizontal snow, to beautiful days in Bergen.

"Palace was totally different to Brann. I'm at a club that expects to win the Toppserien [the Norwegian top-flight] as they believe they have invested the most.

"That's been a real challenge. The WSL is dominated by the favourites in the pack so it wasn't always the expectation to get three points against big teams [at Palace]."

Kaminski admits being away from loved ones is "hard" and she has had to be prepared to "make sacrifices" but Brann's trophy success makes it worth it.

She has also picked up new ideas for her coaching philosophy having experienced the high-risk, attack-minded football in Norway.

"Norwegian teams are almost guaranteed to concede every game because they play such attacking football with no fear, and a relentlessness to press," she added.

"That is a bit different to what I was used to. When I watched the tactical displays when I first came in, I was a little bit alarmed at what people were doing.

"But when you play against their sides, and against that [pressing], it is really difficult. It's given me a lot of fuel for the future.

"There are some really fit, fast and athletic players here. It's not a surprise that big, big clubs are coming in for them."

Female coaches in men's football 'not out of reach'

After a season in Norway, Kaminski believes she is a better coach.

She had spent over 15 years as an assistant manager at various clubs in the WSL 2 and WSL and a coaching role with England's under-19s before joining Palace.

But having added European experience to her CV, Kaminski hopes it will open the door to more opportunities in the future.

"I'd like to think I've got a well-rounded skillset to be able to manage at the top level. Right now, my focus is on Brann and a new chapter," said Kaminski.

"There's only two levels in England that are professional. I definitely wanted to get European exposure, which I was never going to get in England.

"At the time, I was in discussions with a few clubs but it was things that I'd done before, or the project wasn't matching.

"I knew that when I came to Brann, I was going to coach top-level players. I wanted to be at the top of the competition and I was desperate to win a trophy."

Kaminski has urged other female coaches in England to go abroad and gain experience as she believes opportunities are too few in the WSL.

A study from UK Coaching in October showed there has been a 6% decline in the overall number of female coaches in recent years.

There are currently three English female coaches in the WSL - Jo Potter at Crystal Palace, Amy Merricks at Birmingham City and Karen Hills at Charlton Athletic - and they all came up with promoted clubs this summer.

But Kaminski says she is "concerned" about where they might go next and hopes more opportunities in English men's football will open up soon.

"I ended up leaving the country to go and get what I thought I deserved and had earned the right to work in, in terms of the level," said Kaminski.

"There's more than one female out there that's capable [of working in men's football]. I don't think it's out of reach. I would always, certainly, be open to it.

"At the moment, for me, there's not enough consideration even for that opportunity to be given to female managers who are more than capable.

"I think the foundations are there for females to take the plunge but is the world of football ready? I'm unsure."

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal captain's retirement ends extraordinary record-breaking international career which will be debated for years to come
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international duty with Portugal; the 41-year-old earned 234 caps, scoring 146 goals; he won Euro 2016 and two Nations League titles for his country; it comes after a falling out with head coach Jorge Jesus in the last international break
articles.body:
For 23 years he passionately wore the Portugal shirt. The debates about his achievements and legacy representing his country will go on for even longer.

They will primarily focus on two questions. In his pomp, should he have lifted Portugal to greater heights? And in his final years, did he hold the team back from their full potential?

What shouldn't be lost in the analysis - when Ronaldo's record will inevitably be weighed up against that of his great rival (and World Cup winner) Lionel Messi - is that across his unmatched 234 caps, Ronaldo's brilliance helped deliver glory days.

Ronaldo's Portugal era is the most successful era in the country's history.

The Euro 2016 triumph - Portugal's only major tournament win - and the two Nations League titles were moments when he stood in the middle of a nation's celebration, even if injury had forced him to watch the majority of that European Championship final from the sidelines, coaching and cajoling his team-mates with his leg strapped.

The face-off with Zlatan Ibrahimovic in the 2014 World Cup play-off was an epic showdown - and emphatically won by Ronaldo hitting a hat-trick in the second leg to Ibrahimovic's two goals to send Portugal to Russia at Sweden's expense.

"I know Portugal needed me in these matches and I showed that I am here," he said afterwards. And he was almost always there, across six World Cups and six European Championships. Ronaldo matched Pauleta's Portugal scoring record of 47 in 2014 - and then obliterated it, with his final tally at 146.

"I spent my life working to become the best player in the world," Ronaldo said in his international retirement statement. "Today, I realise that my greatest victory was earning the honour of representing the best country in the world."

They are fond words from a man who captained Portugal 172 times. England supporters who remember the 2006 World Cup and Ronaldo's part in the red card for his Manchester United team-mate Wayne Rooney will know how much the national jersey meant to him. The infamous wink underlined where his strongest allegiance lay.

But that meant that Ronaldo, always full of emotion, seemed to feel the blows of international defeat even more emphatically than with his clubs. And, inevitably, across that vast period of time, there were crushing lows.

The image of him breaking down as he exited the 2022 World Cup through the tunnel cruelly captured the pain of falling short on the biggest of stages.

The intensity of focus and pressure on him to deliver in those moments was immense.

"There were also moments when I couldn't give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted," he conceded in his statement on Thursday. "Defeats that still hurt to remember."

A shock loss to Greece in the final of Euro 2004 on home soil in his first tournament playing for his country was an early warning it would not be straightforward. Neither was replicating his prolific club scoring form in the crunch moments.

Ronaldo scored just once in four separate World Cups and his first and only World Cup knockout goal didn't come until this summer, a penalty against Croatia. Did that cost a talented Portugal generation more silverware?

Messi was targeted with similar criticism through the majority of his Argentina career. But that narrative was smashed in recent years. The 2022 World Cup win, two Copa America titles, and a run to another World Cup final this year meant Messi's international career finished at the very top.

Ronaldo's finished with him an unused substitute in Norway, after a summer in which it often seemed his presence in the Portugal XI was to the detriment of the team. At the age of 41, Ronaldo was unable to justify the system still being set up to serve him.

Goncalo Ramos scored the winner against Croatia in injury-time, after Ronaldo had been subbed off. He'd also scored a hat-trick in a 6-1 demolition of Switzerland at the previous World Cup, when Ronaldo had fallen out with coach Fernando Santos and been dropped for the last-16 tie.

Ramos was there scoring the winner in Norway, too, as Ronaldo warmed up, bristling about what he would call broken promises and a breach of trust from Portugal boss Jorge Jesus. He left that last camp early and it was an ugly exit.

Ronaldo's subsequent reveal of the eight points he wanted Jesus to make in an apologetic press conference - including reference to himself as "someone of the stature of Pele or Maradona" - reflected the self-confidence, arrogance and self-centred focus which had propelled him to the very top of the game. But also meant he would never slip down into the role of a squad player.

Such is Ronaldo's enormous profile, his very presence at this summer's World Cup seemed essential to the industry. A red-card ban he'd received against the Republic of Ireland was helpfully cancelled by FIFA, allowing Ronaldo to feature from the first whistle in North America. Portugal's exit to Spain in the last-16 was an anti-climax.

Ronaldo has blown the final whistle now, himself. The Portuguese FA, which gave out the mildest of punishments for his September outburst and walkout , have promised a big send-off. Will there be extra-time? Another runout? Don't bet against it.

Whether Portugal do actually go on to thrive as a more cohesive unit without Ronaldo also remains to be seen. But his was an extraordinary international career which will be etched into history, with his individual records in a Portugal shirt towering high.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland: Seamus Coleman to have 'hybrid role' in upcoming squad
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson says it was "tempting" to include Seamus Coleman in his squad for this month's Nations League matches against Austria and Kosovo despite the defender having not played since June.
articles.body:
Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson said it was "tempting" to include Seamus Coleman in his squad for this month's Nations League matches against Austria and Kosovo despite the defender having not played since June.

Coleman, who has been without a club since leaving Everton in the summer, will instead have what Hallgrimsson called a "hybrid role" in the squad, training with the players but having a "leadership role" alongside the coaching staff.

The 38-year-old has said in recent weeks that he is contemplating retirement but Hallgrimsson said the defender, who has 81 caps, has expressed a desire to "start playing again."

"Coleman is going to be in a hybrid role this camp and he is going to do the sessions with the players but in a leadership role, in a supportive role with us as coaches," Hallgrimsson said after announcing a 24-man squad.

"Hopefully that will get him to start playing again and that is our aim to continue to push him to play. He has expressed he wants to do that.

"Obviously tempting [to include him in the playing squad]. How he did after not playing much for Everton makes us believe he can always do well for the national team. We will have to wait and see."

Captain Nathan Collins has been included after he missed the Republic of Ireland's opening four League B3 matches with a calf injury.

Everton's Mark Travers replaces the injured goalkeeper Gavin Bazanu, who withdrew from the last squad in September saying it "would be wrong to participate" in the fixtures against Israel.

Evan Ferguson (ankle), Josh Cullen (knee) and Jaden Umah (thigh) remain injured and are not included.

Harvey Vale returns to the squad after he missed their previous matches, while Hibernian's Owen Elding will drop to the under-21 squad this window.

Republic of Ireland travel to face Austria in Linz before finishing their Nations League campaign with a home match against Kosovo at Aviva Stadium.

Hallgrimsson's side sit third in League B3 and have won one of their past four games.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo in Saudi Pro League vs Lionel Messi in MLS: Who leads the 2026 club season awards race?
articles.summary: Explore the competition between Cristiano Ronaldo in Saudi Pro League and Lionel Messi in MLS for the 2026 club season awards. Find out their Man of the Match records, scoring stats, and upcoming milestones as they chase individual and team honors after their international retirements.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo has now joined Lionel Messi in bringing his international career to an end, but neither has called time on his playing days. Ronaldo announced his Portugal retirement on Thursday, November 5, and remains active with Al Nassr, where he continues to compete for individual recognition in the Saudi Pro League. Messi, meanwhile, is still leading the charge for Inter Miami in MLS, with his own collection of honours this season. As the two veterans continue their careers at club level, how often have Ronaldo and Messi been recognised as the standout performers in their respective leagues?Cristiano Ronaldo leads Saudi Pro League Man of the Match standingsAccording to the Saudi Pro League, Ronaldo has received the Man of the Match award five times so far this season, more than any other player in the competition. The Al Nassr forward has been recognised after victories over Al Kholood, Al Faisaly, Diriyah, Abha and Al Taawoun.His five awards came in Al Nassr's 5-3 win over Al Kholood, a 3-1 victory away at Al Faisaly, a 3-0 win against Diriyah and two 2-1 victories over Abha and Al Taawoun. The honours reflect his influence across several matches, rather than simply his position among the league's leading goalscorers.Ronaldo has scored eight goals in 10 Saudi Pro League appearances, alongside another goal in two AFC Champions League appearances. His total for Al Nassr stands at nine goals in 12 matches across the two competitions. In the league scoring standings, he is five goals behind Ivan Toney, who leads the race with 13.At 41, Ronaldo is still playing an active role in Al Nassr's campaign. His recent international retirement has not brought his club career to an end, and he remains involved in the pursuit of goals and honours in Saudi Arabia.How many Man of the Match awards does Lionel Messi have in MLS?Messi has been named MLS Player of the Matchday three times in 2026, receiving the award for Matchdays 2, 8 and 23. His most recent recognition came after a particularly productive performance against CF Montreal, when he scored four goals and provided an assist in Inter Miami's 7-1 victory.That award was the 15th MLS Player of the Matchday honour of Messi's career, taking him past Jeff Cunningham into second place in the competition's all-time standings. Only Landon Donovan, who leads the historical list, has won the award more often.There is an important distinction between the two honours, however. The Saudi Pro League awards its Man of the Match to the outstanding player in an individual fixture, whereas MLS selects one Player of the Matchday across all matches played during a round. The MLS recognition is decided through a vote combining media and supporters, making it a different measure of performance.The totals, therefore, cannot be compared directly. Ronaldo's five awards recognise his performances in five separate Saudi Pro League matches, while Messi's three in 2026 represent his selection as the standout player across three entire MLS matchdays. His career total of 15 provides a broader measure of his standing in the league's award history.Messi closes in on MLS playoffs as Ronaldo builds towards another milestoneThe two forwards are also at very different points in their respective club seasons. Ronaldo's Saudi Pro League campaign is still developing, while Messi is approaching the end of the MLS regular season and preparing for the playoffs.Messi has scored 26 goals in 30 MLS matches and leads the Golden Boot race by four goals over FC Dallas forward Petar Musa, who has 22. Inter Miami sit second in the Eastern Conference with 59 points after beating New England 2-1 on November 1. The club have also secured qualification for the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup.Ronaldo, meanwhile, has eight league goals and remains among the Saudi Pro League's leading scorers, although Toney currently holds a five-goal advantage. Across all competitions, his nine goals in 12 appearances have kept him on course for another productive campaign with Al Nassr.Their career totals offer another point of comparison. Ronaldo has scored 985 official senior career goals, leaving him 15 short of the 1,000 mark, while Messi has 936. Ronaldo is still pursuing that landmark with most of his club season ahead, whereas Messi is focused on finishing the MLS campaign and competing for the title.Both remain active at club level after international retirementThe latest developments in their international careers have added a new dimension to the comparison. Messi announced his retirement from international football on August 31, 2026, following Argentina's appearance in the World Cup final. He subsequently played his official farewell match for the national team on October 6, scoring no further international goals in a 3-0 victory over Benin.His decision applies to Argentina, not Inter Miami. Messi remains active in MLS, with his current club contract running through the end of the 2028 season. At 39, he continues to lead the attack as the club prepares for the post-season.Ronaldo has also brought his international career with Portugal to a close, ending with 146 goals in 234 appearances, but he has not retired from professional football altogether. The 41-year-old remains an Al Nassr player and continues to compete in the Saudi Pro League and AFC Champions League.Their international careers may now be behind them, but their club commitments remain very much part of the present. Ronaldo is chasing the 1,000-goal milestone in Saudi Arabia, while Messi is pursuing another MLS title with Inter Miami. Their Man of the Match and Player of the Matchday numbers offer a snapshot of how both continue to shape their teams, even after stepping away from international duty.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Who could Thomas Tuchel select for next England squad? Lankshear, King, Dewsbury-Hall, Henderson, White, Gibbs-White
articles.summary: It's the last international break of the year and England have some big games in the Nations League coming up. Thomas Tuchel has big decisions to make on his next squad selection.
articles.body:
It's the last international break of the year and England have some big games in the Nations League coming up.

After their 7-0 demolition of Croatia in the last match of the Nations League, the Three Lions are all but certain of qualification to the knockout stage.

But, with games at home to Croatia and in Spain to come, they could secure top spot before March's quarter-finals.

Manager Thomas Tuchel likes to reference "credit in the bank" for players who have performed for him in the past.

However, with some of the stars who helped England reach the semi-finals of the World Cup not in the previous squad due to injury issues, it will be interesting to see who Tuchel selects for these two big games after some impressive performances.

The likes of Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice and many others are now stonewall selections but the intrigue is around the remaining few spots still seemingly up for grabs.

Will some old faces earn a recall or will there be new faces soon pulling on the England shirt?

The 19-year-old Fulham midfielder has already been close to a senior-team debut.

King travelled to the US as part of the preparation squad before the World Cup, along with Alex Scott, Ethan Nwaneri and Rio Ngumoha.

Scott and Ngumoha have already made their debuts for the senior side and Nwaneri is currently on loan at Borussia Dortmund.

Tuchel said in his last press conference how King is close to a senior call-up and the midfielder has impressed for the under-21s too.

The biggest challenge for King will be finding a chance to shine in his favoured number 10 position with Bellingham being England's best player and the position being one of real strength for the Three Lions.

There are a lack of number nines in the English game and the job of being Harry Kane's understudy is harder than it sounds.

The England captain has just won the Ballon d'Or, likes to play almost every minute for his country and is the captain, record goalscorer and arguably the best player in Tuchel's side.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has been selected in the squads pre and post the World Cup but, despite doing well for Leeds, it has not quite clicked for him under Tuchel and he was given just 15 minutes in two substitute appearances in the last window.

Tuchel has started to use Bellingham as the back-up to Kane but he could opt for more of a prospect in his squad in this shorter window and turn to Lankshear.

The 21-year-old striker, who like Kane started at Tottenham before being sold to Middlesbrough this summer for £20m, has scored 15 goals in all competitions so far this campaign.

He has scored 13 goals in as many games in the Championship, helping Middlesbrough to the top of the division.

He only made his debut for the under-21s during the last international window and scored in that game so it would be quite a rise for a player who is not in the Premier League.

Tuchel is aware of Lankshear and with a lack of number nines across the age groups it could be an interesting option for a manager who is not afraid of making big calls.

He did miss Middlesbrough's loss to Wrexham on Wednesday with a tweaked hamstring but could return in time for Saturday.

The Everton number 10 has turned down call-ups to play for the Republic of Ireland as he focuses on his dream of trying to represent the Three Lions.

He has been one of the Toffees' standout performers having scored two goals and registered two assists in all competitions, helping Everton to seventh in the league.

Dewsbury-Hall, 28, is a clever technician with an eye for a pass and his ability on the ball would likely suit international football.

But team-mate James Garner, who Tuchel called a mini-Valverde, was called up before Dewsbury-Hall when there were dropouts in the last international break with that showing perhaps he has more to do to get on Tuchel's radar.

Morgan Gibbs-White was probably the unluckiest player to be left out of the initial squad last time around when Tuchel got his players together in September.

But the Nottingham Forest midfielder was called up as a late replacement after a number of high profile pull-outs and left a family holiday to join up with the Three Lions squad.

Tuchel values that kind of dedication and referenced the willingness of Gibbs-White, 26, to join up in the last camp.

The Forest captain featured during every game of the last break although he did not start a game.

But with Forest struggling at the bottom end of the table - and competing against the likes of Bellingham, Phil Foden, Cole Palmer and Eberechi Eze - the midfielder could miss out again.

A must pick or unreliable? Tuchel's Palmer dilemma

White has been unlucky since he ended his international hiatus to return in March.

The Arsenal defender missed the World Cup with a knee injury that saw him also miss the Champions League final.

White then missed the first England squad of this campaign with injury, with Tuchel saying the 29-year-old would have been called up if he had been fit, citing his partnership with Bukayo Saka as potentially good for the Three Lions.

But White has been available for all but one of Arsenal's games this season and would add a quality defensive option at right-back if selected, especially with Reece James missing through injury.

Jordan Henderson has not been in the England set-up since the World Cup, where he fell over an advertising hoarding following England's win over Mexico in the Azteca Stadium and broke his arm.

Many would have thought the 36-year-old's international career was over but Henderson, then at Brentford, made a move to Chelsea as they looked to add experience to their young squad.

After recovering from the arm injury, Henderson has surprised some to become an important part of the Chelsea midfield, starting five games in a row and scoring twice in a win over Bournemouth, before he missed the Blues' win over Manchester United with injury.

Henderson is a popular figure, respected by staff and players and is again performing at the top level.

articles.title: Quique: "Lo que más nos preocupa ahora es recuperar la moral de los jugadores"
articles.standfirst: El técnico madrileño confía en lograr una victoria antes del parón para cortar la dinámica negativa del equipo
articles.summary: El técnico madrileño confía en lograr una victoria antes del parón para cortar la dinámica negativa del equipo
articles.body: Quique Sánchez Flores ofreció su comparecencia más apagada desde que está en Vitoria. Los diferentes acontecimientos en forma de tragedias han cambiado el semblante del técnico madrileño, que se centra en poder revertir la situación del Alavés antes del parón y lograr un triunfo este viernes en el Sánchez-Pizjuán que les permita poner fin a las siete jornadas sin ganar. Jesús de Miguel: "Estamos con mucho dolor y tristeza. Hemos notado el impacto en el ánimo del grupo porque es la pérdida de un compañero. Le mandamos el pésame a los familiares y los amigos". Owono: "Tenía pensado hablar con él, pero no lo he hecho porque es muy pronto. Está en su momento de soledad, aceptando la realidad. Los accidentes son accidentes y con una víctima es suficiente. Ha sido una concatenación de hechos catastróficos. Owono tendrá que seguir y probablemente es algo de lo que no se va a recuperar, pero tendrá que pensar que la vida continúa y seguir manifestándose en el futuro de la mejor forma posible". Sánchez Pizjuán: "Lo que más nos preocupa ahora es recuperar la moral de los jugadores. Más allá de las rachas y las clasificaciones, queremos recuperarles porque son los que tienen que sacar esto adelante. Mañana vamos a un ambiente de mucha tensión, donde el Sevilla nos va a hacer un partido complicado, con una afición que aprieta muchísimo y va a ser una prueba muy importante". Convocatoria: "Excepto Mikel y Facundo, todos los demás van a estar". Aspectos de mejora: "Cuando hay confusión tienes que volver a lo más simple y buscar los recursos más sencillos. No podemos irnos al grueso que queríamos llegar cuando empezamos a descender, sino recuperar las cosas más sencillas que nos hacían ser tan competitivos en el inicio". Intensidad y contundencia: "Es algo que se puede entrenar. Cuando pones a los jugadores en espacios más reducidos buscas que choquen. Hay que dar un soplido más allá de lo que nos llega con el estado de ánimo. Tenemos que hacer ese esfuerzo y esa visión". Guridi: "Le utilicé mucho porque consideraba que era un jugador muy de nuestro perfil. La Dirección Deportiva trabajó para que se quedara y se hizo un esfuerzo para ello, pero él quería explorar otras cosas y lo entendimos. Se portó muy bien con nosotros y le deseamos lo mejor a partir de mañana". Sevilla: "Destaco a su afición. Es magnífica y se portaron de maravilla con nosotros. También destaco sus medios de comunicación, que tuvimos una conexión magnífica. Tuvimos una buena relación con su presidente, que es un tipo que se preocupa mucho por su equipo. Es un gran club. Cuando llegas por Sevilla te pasan por la sala donde tienen todos los trofeos que han conseguido a lo largo de su historia. Esa grandeza se respira cuando llegas". Situación personal: "Llevamos dos semanas muy fastidiadas. Más allá de que nos gusta ganar, pero a nivel moral y de sociedad estamos absolutamente golpeados. Me ha costado mucho sacar una sonrisa".

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo retires from Portugal national team
articles.summary: The 41-year-old released a video letter on Thursday morning announcing his international retirement.
articles.body:
( WCMH ) – Cristiano Ronaldo has decided he has played his last game for the Portugal national team.

The 41-year-old released a video letter on Thursday morning announcing his international retirement after scoring a record 146 goals for Portugal in a record 255 games for his country.

“It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the head alone. They are also made with the heart,” Ronaldo said. “I am bringing to an end a journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever.”

The soccer star, a native of the small island of Madeira, played his first game for Portugal on Aug. 20, 2003, against Kazakhstan and his last on Sept. 27, 2026, against Norway. Between those games is a legacy unlike any other in sports.

Ronaldo, nicknamed CR7, led the European nation to its first major international trophy in 2016 at the UEFA Euros. Despite leaving the final against France injured, Ronaldo was the first to lift the trophy after a 1-0 win in extra time. Portugal also won two UEFA Nations League titles with Ronaldo as the captain in 2019 and 2025. His 14 goals across six Euro tournaments are the most of all time.

While CR7 never lifted a World Cup trophy, he is the only man to score at six different World Cups with 11 goals across those tournaments. His first was a penalty against Iran in the 2006 group stage, with his last coming in 2026 from a penalty against Croatia in the Round of 32. He also represented his country at the 2004 Olympics in Athens.

Ronaldo is still continuing his club career with Saudi team Al Nassr and announced his international retirement less than one week after scoring a hattrick against Al Kholood. He has seven goals this season for Al Nassr.

Portugal will continue life without Ronaldo in this year’s Nations League as it looks to defend its 2025 title. The first tournament Portugal will play without Ronaldo is the 2028 Euros before the nation is a co-host for the 2030 FIFA World Cup .

articles.title: UF Reportedly Expected to Make QB1 Change, Start Tramell Jones Jr. vs. Oklahoma
articles.summary: Florida is planning to go back to Tramell Jones Jr. at quarterback with Aaron Philo continuing to deal with a shoulder injury.
articles.body:
Florida is planning to go back to Tramell Jones Jr. at quarterback with Aaron Philo continuing to deal with a shoulder injury.

Per Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports, Jones is expected to start for the Gators on Saturday against Oklahoma.

Philo originally injured his shoulder in Florida's loss to South Carolina on Oct. 10. He sat out the win over Texas seven days later, with Jones making his first career start in that game.

Jones finished 22-of-35 for 155 yards with two touchdowns through the air. He added another 41 rushing yards on 10 carries to help the Gators pull off the upset against then-No. 7 Texas in Austin.

After the Gators' bye week, Philo returned as the starter against Georgia on Oct. 31. He struggled with two interceptions on seven pass attempts in the first half, prompting head coach Jon Sumrall to bench him for Jones.

Jones, who was listed as questionable early last week due to an undisclosed injury, didn't fare much better against a ferocious Bulldogs defense. He went 18-of-25 for 172 yards with one interception in a 27-8 loss.

Sumrall has said Jones' injury might require offseason surgery, but he appears to be good enough to take the reins for the offense as the Gators look to get back on track.

A 4-star recruit in the 2025 class, Jones has appeared in nine games through his first two seasons at Florida. He is completing 67.7 percent of his attempts for 770 yards, six touchdowns and three interceptions.

Florida is ranked No. 25 in the AP poll with a 5-3 record, including marquee wins over Texas and Mississippi. A victory over Oklahoma (4-4) will make the Gators bowl eligible after going 4-8 last season.

The Gators and Sooners kickoff on Saturday at 7:45 p.m. ET from Ben Hill Griffin Stadium.

articles.title: Zaragoza y Huesca se reencuentran sin los dos últimos grandes protagonistas
articles.standfirst: El sábado se enfrentan en el Ibercaja Estadio por primera vez tras sus descensos
articles.summary: El sábado se enfrentan en el Ibercaja Estadio por primera vez tras sus descensos
articles.body: Este sábado, Real Zaragoza y Huesca viven su segundo derbi aragonés del curso tras haberse medido ya al Teruel cada uno. Eso sí, en este hay más picante por la rivalidad surgida en los últimos años y el descenso que ambos vivieron en la pasada campaña. Además, será la primera vez que se enfrenten tras lo sucedido en el polémico y último cara a cara que tuvo lugar en El Alcoraz. Los dos máximos protagonistas de aquel entonces no estarán mañana. Todavía se recuerda la agresión de Esteban Andrada sobre Jorge Pulido por la actitud del defensa durante todo el encuentro. Un puñetazo que dio la vuelta al mundo. El argentino recibió una dura sanción de 13 partidos y no volvió a jugar más con el cuadro maño. Regresó al Monterrey al acabar su cesión y se ha quedado en tierras mexicanas. Mientras que Pulido firmó por el Almería, algo que ya anunció en las pasadas navidades y generó mucho revuelo. Los andaluces no ascendieron y el central se quedó sin el sueño de jugar en Primera pero sí lo está haciendo en uno de los máximos aspirantes a volver a la máxima categoría del fútbol español. Esta vez los focos estarán puestos en otros jugadores y en las figuras de Ibai Gómez y Albert Rudé. El vasco tiene al Real Zaragoza colíder y ha devuelto la ilusión. Por su parte, el catalán ha logrado revertir la situación de los azulgranas que vuelven a mirar hacia arriba. A buen seguro que la tensión estará mucho más rebajada respecto al último derbi. Los dos equipos querrán dar un golpe en la mesa y no en el adversario.

articles.title: Jesus de Miguel: Funeral of Tenerife forward takes place as family thankful for support
articles.summary: Jesus de Miguel's family say "the mark he has left on so many people" is something they will always remember as the footballer's funeral takes place in Spain.
articles.body:
Jesus de Miguel's family said "the mark he has left on so many people" was something they would always remember as the footballer's funeral took place on Thursday.

The Tenerife forward, who was 30, died after suffering a serious injury during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

After colliding with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono, De Miguel lay motionless on the pitch while being treated by medical staff and was taken to hospital, where he died at 07:00 GMT on Tuesday.

Owono was sent off for the challenge and the game was abandoned.

De Miguel's funeral was held in his parents' hometown of Navahermosa, Toledo, about 125km from the Spanish capital Madrid.

His Tenerife team-mates carried his casket before the service at San Miguel Arcangel.

Current Spain coach Luis de la Fuente was among the mourners, along with Real Madrid president Florentino Perez, Atletico Madrid chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin and former Real and Spain coach Jose Antonio Camacho.

De Miguel's agent, Manuel Hernandez, issued a statement on behalf of the family, which read: "Thank you for loving him, for remembering him and for being with us.

"We cannot find enough words to thank you for every message, every phone call and every gesture of affection we are receiving.

"Feeling such affection for Jesus and seeing the mark he has left on so many people is something we will always carry with us.

"Jesus leaves a void that is impossible to fill, but also cherished memories for all of us who were fortunate enough to share our lives with him."

Tributes have been paid to De Miguel, who joined Tenerife in the summer of 2025, with a minute's silence being held at all games in European competitions this week.

In a statement issued by his club Andorra on Wednesday, goalkeeper Owono said he was experiencing "the most difficult days of my life".

"I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus," he added. "I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him."

The family also asked "with the utmost respect, that our privacy - and that of everyone who is supporting us at this time - be respected".

In the hours after the death was announced, mourners laid flowers and lit candles beneath a black and white image of De Miguel at the Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez - the stadium on the island of Tenerife, where Monday's game took place.

"We need to grieve in the peace and quiet that this situation demands," the statement added.

"We appreciate the affection, concern and expressions of support that his loss is inspiring, and we are deeply grateful to you all."

Players want all matches postponed this weekend

The Spanish footballers' union, the AFE, made a request on Thursday for all this weekend's matches to be postponed out of respect for De Miguel.

Tenerife's match at Granada and Andorra's game against Mallorca have already been postponed, as were several midweek cup fixtures.

However, all Spanish sides in European competition have played their games this week.

The AFE said of the weekend games: "The footballers have expressed their deep sorrow for this loss and do not believe that there are the psychological and humane conditions necessary for the competition to be played in normal circumstances."

The union said its members "in every category" believed "unanimously" that the matches should not be played.

articles.title: Gianni Infantino: FIFA president faces challenge from Japan FA chief Kohzo Tashima in 2027 election
articles.summary: Gianni Infantino faces his first serious challenger for the FIFA presidency; Japan FA honorary president Kohzo Tashima intends to stand in next March's election; UEFA is expected to back him if he is the only challenger
articles.body:
Tashima, a member of the FIFA Council and honorary president of the Japan Football Association (JFA), will have the backing of his national association and is expected to secure the five endorsements required to become an official candidate.

UEFA is working to prevent Infantino from securing another term and is expected to overwhelmingly back Tashima if he emerges as the incumbent's only challenger.

In that scenario, the Japanese could also attract support from anti-Infantino factions within the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF.

The AFC's position remains significant, with president Sheikh Salman having performed a U-turn to back Infantino at the confederation's Congress two weeks ago.

FIFA's 211 member associations will vote in the election, with a candidate requiring at least 106 votes to win. The deadline for candidates to declare their intention to stand is November 18.

Tashima is a former Japan international who went on to coach the country's Under-17 and Under-20 national teams before moving into football administration.

He has held several senior positions within the JFA, including general secretary, vice-president and president, and has also served on the AFC's executive committee.

Can Tashima beat Infantino and could Wenger enter the race?

"Kozo Tashima certainly gives Gianni Infantino something to worry about. I think Infantino would much prefer to stand unopposed.

"Having said that, I'm not sure whether Tashima will get the support he needs to beat Infantino.

"You have to remember how FIFA's presidential election works. FIFA has 211 members, and each national association has one vote. So you need the backing of 106 FAs to win.

"Now, I think Tashima, if he is Infantino's only challenger, will have the overwhelming backing of Europe. He can count on almost all of UEFA's 55 votes.

"He'll also pick up some votes in Asia, even though the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), his own confederation, has backed Infantino. Its president, Sheikh Salman, performed a U-turn two weeks ago. Originally, he was anti-Infantino, but at the confederation's Congress he announced they would back the FIFA president.

"But that doesn't mean all of Asia are going to support Infantino. So I think Tashima can pick up some support there as well. He can also attract backing in CONCACAF, across North and Central America, and perhaps a few votes in the Caribbean. Can he get to 106? I'm not so sure.

"What we need to look out for over the next two weeks is whether anybody else emerges.

"There's been lots of talk about Arsene Wenger potentially entering the race. He's a legendary figure in football, somebody who, of course, used to manage Arsenal. At the moment, he's FIFA's chief of global football development.

"I think if he were to come out and stand, that would make real, real headlines. That would be front-page news.

"I'm not sure if he'd have the numbers to beat Infantino either, but I think he would have a good chance, especially because lots of things can happen in FIFA presidential elections.

"For instance, when Infantino first won the presidency 10 years ago, he was not the favourite. He wasn't even supposed to be a candidate. The only reason he entered the race was that Michel Platini had to drop out.

"So lots of things can change. At the moment, it looks like Infantino is the favourite, despite all the controversies and scandals. But watch this space, because sometimes FIFA presidential elections can be very, very exciting."

articles.title: Ronaldo in records: International milestones from the football icon
articles.summary: Ronaldo, 41, ended an illustrious 23-year career that spanned six World Cups and six European Championships.
articles.body:
Portuguese football legend Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football , where he has left an indelible mark as one of the sport’s greatest players.

The 41-year-old, who has played 234 times for Portugal and scored 146 goals, holds the all-time record for international appearances and international goals.

He ended an illustrious 23-year career that spanned six World Cups and six European Championships.

When did Ronaldo make his debut for Portugal?

Ronaldo made his senior debut for Portugal aged 18 in a friendly against Kazakhstan, coming on as a half-time substitute for Luis Figo.

He wore a number 17 jersey at the time since 7 was claimed by Figo. It was only after Figo’s retirement in 2006 that Ronaldo staked claim to the jersey full-time and made it synonymous with his brand CR7.

When did Ronaldo play his last match for Portugal?

Ronaldo’s last appearance for Portugal was on September 24 in a 1-0 win over Wales, where he was substituted in the 67th minute.

Coach Jorge Jesus’s decision to keep him on the bench in the following match was a catalyst for the explosive falling out and subsequent departure from national duty, for which he was suspended for 30 days and fined 255 euros ($285).

Ronaldo has a final chance to upgrade his international statistics when Portugal, who top Nations League Group A4, host second second-placed Denmark on November 14 in Braga before visiting Wales in their final two group games.

Over on the club side, his next match with Al-Nassr in the Saudi Pro League is on November 20 against Al-Qadsiah.

What records does Ronaldo hold with Portugal?

Ronaldo has an encyclopaedia worth of records in football, most notably as the world’s all-time international goalscorer (146 goals) and the most capped international player (234 appearances).

He has scored for Portugal in 23 consecutive calendar years (2004-2026) and is the country’s top scorer at the World Cup with 11 goals in 27 tournament games.

The statistics do not do justice to how Ronaldo helped Portugal reach new heights and make the European nation a regular presence at major tournaments.

He captained Portugal to its first major title at Euro 2016, followed by the Nations League trophy in 2019 and 2025.

Under his watch, Portugal qualified for the World Cup every single time; prior to that they had only reached the tournaments in 1966, 1986, and 2002.

Similarly, at the Euros, Portugal had appeared only three times before Ronaldo: 1984, 1996 and 2000. After he arrived, they qualified for every edition.

What international records does Ronaldo have?

Ronaldo became the first player to reach 200 men’s international appearances when he played against Iceland in a 2024 UEFA Euro qualifying match.

He was also the first player to score 100 international goals for a European national team. He became the first player to score 10 international hat-tricks, a record Lionel Messi eclipsed with 11 during Argentina’s 3-0 win over Algeria at the World Cup.

Last summer saw Ronaldo become the first player to both play and score in six different World Cups, starting with his debut against Angola in 2006 and scoring his first goal in the tournament against Iran. His final World Cup goal came from the penalty kick scored against Croatia in the round of 32 in 2026.

He also became the oldest player to score in a World Cup knockout match, aged 41 years and 147 days.

On the European side, Ronaldo holds records for most European Championship tournaments played (6), most appearances (30), and most goals (14).

articles.title: Oliver Glasner: Nottingham Forest head coach says post-Brentford outburst was meant positively
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner has offered further insight into his post-Brentford outburst; Forest have won just once this season and sit 19th in the Premier League; watch Forest vs Man City live on Saturday Night Football from 5pm; kick-off 5.30pm
articles.body:
The head coach went on two explosive rants to Sky Sports and in his post-match press conference after defeat at the Gtech Community Stadium which left Forest 19th in the league.

Among other things, Glasner said: "We have to accept it's not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it's not good enough. And that's why for me, it's now time that we change things, that I change things, and that's what I will do.

"I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it's always compromises. It's a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in."

Nottingham Forest have won just once this season after the Austrian's summer arrival, losing four of the last five.

When asked what the reaction has been since the weekend outburst, Glasner said in a press conference ahead of facing Manchester City this weekend, live on Sky Sports : "A good training week - this was the consequence. This is what I hope, what we all expected from each other to try hard, to get better results at the end."

The head coach went on to offer more insight into why he reacted in the way he did, adding that if you do not point out problems, things cannot begin to change.

"This is just how I am. If I see things I don't like, I will let you know and if I see things I really like, I will let you know as well," he said.

"If I feel I need to shake things up, then I will. If I feel I need to keep quiet, then I will.

"With the four or five games we lost, I can't continue telling the same story - 'good start, well played, missed chances, making mistakes, losing. OK, on to next week'.

"That's also why I needed to change what I'm telling and to be aware of things because otherwise maybe we will always keep going in the same way, and we'll think 'oh, why don't things change?' and that was the reason.

"I didn't attack somebody directly, but it's all about what we all share. We share that we want to be successful, that we want to win games and that we are doing better than we did.

"That's why there was not a problem. It was much louder outside than I felt it was inside.

"This is just how I see a relationship has to be... if you don't say something, the other person will never know.

"Then I can't blame somebody because if they don't know, how can things change? We are now in a society where maybe criticism or the way I talked was in a negative way, but the intention is positive.

"The intention is to change something and get better results, then we all have a better life."

Glasner refused to be drawn on what exact changes he has seen this week, adding 'It's like Las Vegas - what happens in Las Vegas stays in Las Vegas'.

However, he did offer a small elaboration, saying: "Maybe I'm doing a bit more talking to the players in general and talking to them individually... but it's always in a positive way.

"This is what I want everyone to understand. I never do anything to punish somebody, why should I? But it's either to shake things up or to tell somebody what we need to improve. It's clear for everyone that we need to improve, especially our results. That was why I reacted in that way."

When asked whether he was surprised that he has had to have these conversations with players, Glasner replied: "I'm not surprised... One of the biggest goals I have is to create a culture and an environment where you want to be, but where you also want to work hard.

"We are not a spa and wellness hotel, but we are also not the military, and we need to find the in between. I want to get every player having this intrinsic motivation to his game... I would like to be challenged by the players that they can ask: what can I improve?

"Because everything that comes from the players, it's 100 times more worth it than when it comes from the manager or from the staff. Sometimes it seems to be that it always has to come from the coaching side."

articles.title: Camp Nou: miedo a más retrasos
articles.standfirst: El Barça negocia con Limak nuevas penalizaciones si no cumple plazos
articles.summary: El Barça negocia con Limak nuevas penalizaciones si no cumple plazos
articles.body: El Barcelona afrontará al final de la temporada la etapa decisiva de las obras del Spotify Camp Nou. Una vez que dispute el último partido de esta campaña, comenzarán los últimos grandes trabajos en el estadio. El más importante será la instalación de la cubierta sobre las gradas. Se trata de una obra compleja y de difícil ejecución que, según las previsiones, tardará unos seis meses en completarse. Por este motivo, el Barcelona ya ha solicitado al Ayuntamiento el uso del Estadi Olímpic de Montjuïc, donde podrá disputar sus partidos hasta el mes de enero. A partir de ese momento, tendría que regresar a su estadio, con la cubierta ya instalada. Además, hay otras dos actuaciones muy importantes que se llevarán a cabo de forma paralela: la construcción de la nueva tienda del Barcelona y la finalización del resto de los asientos VIP. Estas tres actuaciones son claves porque afectan directamente a la economía del club. Los ingresos del Barcelona la próxima temporada dependerán en gran medida de que pueda disponer de un mayor aforo una vez instalada la cubierta, lo que permitirá alcanzar los 95.000 espectadores. También serán fundamentales la comercialización de los palcos, una importante fuente de ingresos, y las ventas de productos oficiales en la tienda. Por este motivo, el Barcelona está negociando con Limak un nuevo contrato en el que se establecerán importantes penalizaciones por cualquier retraso que se produzca en las obras, como ya sucedió durante la primera fase de los trabajos en el estadio, según informó La Vanguardia. El regreso al Camp Nou se fue demorando de manera paulatina porque las obras no estaban finalizadas. La directiva no quiere que esta situación vuelva a repetirse. Además, el club prevé cerrar en las próximas semanas la nueva financiación de las obras. La Asamblea de socios aprobó una ampliación de 300 millones de euros que está a punto de formalizarse. Para el Barcelona es muy importante que no se produzcan retrasos, ya que necesita cumplir el presupuesto aprobado en dicha Asamblea, que contempla los ingresos derivados del mayor aforo del estadio, los palcos y la nueva tienda.

articles.title: Las dos caras del Atlético
articles.standfirst: Más derrotas en 4 partidos de Champions que en 11 de Liga. Los datos en todos los apartados enseñan dos equipos distintos
articles.summary: Más derrotas en 4 partidos de Champions que en 11 de Liga. Los datos en todos los apartados enseñan dos equipos distintos
articles.body: Dos caras, como si fueran el doctor Jekyll y Mr. Hyde, como si lo que cuaja en fin de semana de Liga se destruyera durante la semana de Champions. Así, con dos caras, es el Atlético de la temporada 26-27 cuando se han disputado 15 partidos: 11 domésticos y cuatro cruzando los Pirineos. Los números, otras veces poco significativos en el mundo del fútbol no tan dado a la estadística como otros deportes, arrojan dos vertientes casi antagónicas. El principal, los puntos ganados, es quizá el resumen de todo lo que vendrá después. Mientras en España se han logrado 28 de los 33 puntos (2,5 por choque) en Europa apenas 4 en 4 (1 por partido). Las derrotas son otro buen ejemplo. En LaLiga solo el Athletic ha dejado sin sumar a los madrileños en 11 partidos. En Europa se han producido el doble de derrotas: dos en apenas cuatro encuentros. El doble con casi un tercio de partidos jugados. No es menos significativo el porcentaje de triunfos: el Atleti gana el 81,82% de partidos nacionales y apenas el 25 continentales. La producción ofensiva se dobla en España respecto a Europa. Mientras en el primero marca dos goles por encuentro, 22 en 11, en el segundo apenas 1 por choque. Sólo ante el Manchester United mejoró esa cifra pero ante el Bayern se quedó a cero. Poco acierto hablando de los mejores equipos de Europa. Pero todo tiene una explicación, en el caso del ataque es que se remata menos en Champions (9,75 por 17,27), se regatea menos (6 por 9,45) se tiran menos córners (3,75 a 5,73) y también se tiene menos el esférico (50 en Europa por 58,81). Esto último, claro, también explica los motivos por los que se encajan más goles (1,25 a 0,73). Así, con esta doble realidad llega el domingo el Barça al Metropolitano. En juego, ni más ni menos, que el liderato de una Liga que tiene a los tres primeros en apenas tres puntos. A los de Flick les vale con sumar para mantenerse en lo más alto, mientras que los de Simeone necesitan ganar para olvidar el traspiés continental que le deja en una posición complicada: el top 8 está casi imposible y de no empezar a sumar de tres a tres será también difícil llegar a los cruces antes de octavos. Líder y decepción rotunda, las dos caras de este Atlético.

articles.title: Swansea City: Stephen Welsh, Eom Jisung and Moussa Yeo injury boosts before Birmingham City
articles.summary: Swansea City receive major fitness boost as influential centre-back Stephen Welsh is cleared of serious injury.
articles.body:
Swansea City have received a major fitness boost after influential centre-back Stephen Welsh was cleared of serious injury.

Swansea feared the Scotland international had suffered knee ligament damage following a challenge from Ebou Adams during Tuesday's 3-1 defeat at Portsmouth.

But scans have revealed Welsh has no significant problem, meaning he may even be able to play some part at Birmingham City on Saturday.

There is more positive news from the treatment room going into the weekend, with wingers Moussa Yeo and Eom Jisung fit to return against Chris Davies' in-form Blues side.

However, midfielder Stephen Eustaquio will again be absent due to a groin problem and Melker Widell is out with a minor hamstring injury which meant he was withdrawn at half-time at Fratton Park.

"Welshy's scan is clear. It's just really a bad knock so there's nothing major," said Swansea head coach Vitor Matos.

"We will still assess if he will be available for Saturday, but it's not a bad injury. It's just a knock that is really, really painful."

Matos says a decision is yet to be taken on whether Welsh, 26, will join up with Scotland in the international break which follows the Birmingham game.

Eustaquio, who came off injured during last weekend's win over Blackburn, has been withdrawn from Canada duty, with Swansea hoping the former Porto player may be fit for their game against West Bromwich Albion on Saturday, 21 November.

Widell is expected back for the Baggies' visit, while Yeo returns this weekend having missed Swansea's past three matches with a hamstring issue and Eom is back in contention after a knock suffered against Blackburn last weekend.

Matos revealed Ben Cabango did not train in the lead-up to Portsmouth because of a fitness issue, hence he was on the bench before coming on to replace Welsh, but Swansea's captain is available for Birmingham.

"In this moment unfortunately we are having a few knocks and that creates a little bit of instability regarding the starting XI and the availability of players," Matos added.

"You need to learn how to deal with the situations and that's it. It's hard to manage, but we will find a way of course."

articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars will be facing the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday Night Football, as they look to continue to add to their win total. They've played well on both sides of the ball this season, but it's been the offense that has been able to have a lot of success, and Trevor Lawrence is getting everyone involved.

As for the Ravens, they haven't been able to have much consistency because of injuries, specifically to their quarterbacks. After returning from injury last week, Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury on the first play of the game and was ruled out. Tyler Huntley then came in, and he suffered turf toe, which will cause him to miss the rest of the season. That means that Joe Fagnano will start against the Jaguars.

The Jaguars have a few injuries coming into this game, with Bhayshul Tuten being one of them. He's been dealing with a foot and ankle injury and hasn't practiced all week because of it. Nonetheless, he's still listed as questionable for the game, but it's hard to see him suiting up if he hasn't practiced. Tuten is supposed to be a game-time decision , so his status is truly up in the air right now.
